definition_en: a line of metal rings joined together; a series of connected things; to fasten with a chain
core_image: 一环扣一环，拉起头就带动了尾
scene: 门口的自行车被铁环一圈圈锁在栏杆上。 Someone locked my bike with a heavy chain to the rail.
sceneCN: 这里 chain 是「链条」（第 1 个义项：金属环相连）；句意是有人用粗链条把我的自行车锁在栏杆上。

senses.title: Metal rings joined together
senses.definition: a line of metal rings linked together, used for locking or pulling
senses.definitionCN: 金属环连成一串，用于锁系或拉拽
senses.example: The dog pulled against its chain.
senses.exampleCN: 狗拽着拴它的链子。
senses.why: Rings threaded one through the next make a flexible strong line.
senses.whyCN: 一环穿过一环，便形成柔韧而结实的线。

senses.title: A connected series
senses.definition: things joined one after another, like events or mountains
senses.definitionCN: 一件接一件相连的事物，如事件或山脉
senses.example: A chain of delays made us miss the train.
senses.exampleCN: 一连串的延误使我们误了火车。
senses.why: Events, like rings, hook onto each other.
senses.whyCN: 事件像环一样彼此钩连。

senses.title: Shops under one company
senses.definition: a group of shops owned by one company
senses.definitionCN: 由一家公司拥有的多家商店
senses.example: A new coffee chain opened near our school.
senses.exampleCN: 一家新的咖啡连锁店在我们学校附近开业。
senses.why: Each shop is a ring on the company's long line.
senses.whyCN: 每家店都是公司长线上的一环。

senses.title: To fasten with a chain
senses.definition: to tie something with a chain so it cannot move
senses.definitionCN: 用链条拴住使其无法移动
senses.example: They chained the gates shut during the holiday.
senses.exampleCN: 假期里他们用链条把大门锁上。
senses.why: The object becomes one more ring held in place.
senses.whyCN: 被锁之物成了被固定住的又一环。

definition_zh: 坏的；有害的；严重的；腐坏的
definition_en: of low quality, or harmful, or serious, or no longer fresh
core_image: 观众看到一半就离场的电影院
scene: 电影院里，观众看到一半就陆续离场。 The film was bad, so we left early.
sceneCN: 这里 bad 是「坏的」（第 1 个义项：质量差、不好）；句意为电影很糟，所以我们提前离场。

pos.zh: 形容词：坏的；有害的；严重的；腐坏的

senses.title: Of low quality
senses.definition: of low quality or not good
senses.definitionCN: 质量差或不好
senses.example: The film was bad, so we left early.
senses.exampleCN: 电影很糟，所以我们提前离场。
senses.why: The old word simply named what is not good, so poor quality is the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 古词只表示「不好」，所以质量差就是第一义。

senses.title: Harmful
senses.definition: harmful or likely to cause trouble
senses.definitionCN: 有害或容易带来麻烦
senses.example: Too much sugar is bad for your teeth.
senses.exampleCN: 糖吃太多对牙齿有害。
senses.why: What is not good can also work against a person, which gives the sense of harmful.
senses.whyCN: 不好的东西也可能对人不利，于是有「有害」的义项。

senses.title: Serious
senses.definition: serious or severe in degree
senses.definitionCN: 程度严重或厉害
senses.example: He has a bad cold.
senses.exampleCN: 他得了重感冒。
senses.why: A thing that fails badly can fail in a large degree, which gives the sense of serious.
senses.whyCN: 坏起来的东西也可能坏得很厉害，于是有「严重」的义项。

senses.title: No longer fresh
senses.definition: no longer fresh and fit to eat
senses.definitionCN: 不再新鲜、不宜食用
senses.example: The milk has gone bad.
senses.exampleCN: 牛奶变质了。
senses.why: Food that has stopped being what it should be is called bad, which gives the spoiled sense.
senses.whyCN: 食物不再保持应有的样子就被叫作 bad，于是有「变质」的义项。

definition_zh: 一点；小块；一会儿；（计算机）比特
definition_en: a small piece or amount of something, a short time, or the smallest unit of data in computing
core_image: 从一整块面包上掰下来的一小角
scene: 餐桌上，孩子从整块面包上掰下一小块递给妹妹。 He tore off a bit of bread and gave it to her.
sceneCN: 这里 bit 是「一点；小块」（第 1 个义项：从整体上分出的一小部分）；句意为他掰下一小块面包递给她。

pos.zh: 名词：一点；小块；一会儿；比特
动词：bite 的过去式，义为「咬」

derivatives.zh: 由 bit 加 -y 构成，义为「零碎的；琐碎的」

由 bit 与 stream 组合而成，义为「位流；比特流」

senses.title: A small piece
senses.definition: a small piece cut or broken off from something larger
senses.definitionCN: 从较大的东西上切下或掰下的一小块
senses.example: He gave me a bit of his chocolate.
senses.exampleCN: 他给了我一点他的巧克力。
senses.why: Old English bita meant the piece bitten off, so the first sense is a fragment taken from something bigger.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 bita 指被咬下来的一块，所以第一个义项就是从较大物体上取下的一小份。

senses.title: A small amount
senses.definition: a small amount of a substance or of a quality
senses.definitionCN: 少量物质，或某种性质的一点点
senses.example: Add a bit of salt to the soup.
senses.exampleCN: 往汤里加一点盐。
senses.why: The same piece image is used for an amount you cannot count, such as salt or patience.
senses.whyCN: 同一幅「小块」的画面被用在数不清的少量事物上，比如盐或耐心。

senses.title: A short time
senses.definition: a short period of time
senses.definitionCN: 很短的一段时间
senses.example: Wait a bit before you open the door.
senses.exampleCN: 等一会儿再开门。
senses.why: A small piece of time is still a piece: the word cuts a short slice out of the day.
senses.whyCN: 一小段时间同样是一小份：这个词从一天里切出短短的一截。

senses.title: The binary unit
senses.definition: the smallest unit of information in a computer, either zero or one
senses.definitionCN: 计算机中最小的信息单位，取值只能是零或一
senses.example: One bit can hold only zero or one.
senses.exampleCN: 一个比特只能存零或一。
senses.why: Computer science took the word for a small piece and made it the smallest possible piece of data.
senses.whyCN: 计算机科学借用了「一小块」这个词，把它变成数据里最小的一块。

items.en: Later the same word was used for a short time and for a small amount of anything.

items.en: In the twentieth century computing gave bit a technical sense: the smallest unit of data.
items.cn: 二十世纪的计算机领域给 bit 一个技术义：最小的数据单位。

root: bit 来自古英语 bita，意思是「咬下来的一块」，源自动词 bitan（咬），这个词也给出今天的 bite。名词从中古英语的短形式 bit 一路保留，先指食物的一小块，后扩展到少量与片刻，二十世纪又成为计算机里最小的数据单位。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses of bit rest on one picture: a small piece taken off something larger.
sensesIntro.cn: bit 的四个义项都立在同一个画面上：从更大物体上取下的一小块。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a corner torn off a loaf of bread
core.cn: 核心意象：从整条面包上撕下的一角

branches.en: THE PIECE: a fragment cut or torn from something larger keeps the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 小块线：从较大物体上切下或撕下的一点，保留最古老的义项。

branches.en: THE AMOUNT: salt and patience are measured with the same small piece.
branches.cn: 数量线：盐和耐心都用同一「一小块」来计量。

branches.en: THE MOMENT: a short slice of time is a small piece of the day.
branches.cn: 时间线：一天里切出的短短一截，就是一小份时间。

branches.en: THE DATA: computing turned the small piece into the smallest unit of information.
branches.cn: 数据线：计算机把这一小块变成最小的信息单位。

branches.en: THE FRAGMENT: a countable piece and an uncountable amount share one image.
branches.cn: 碎块线：可数的一小块与不可数的少量共享同一幅画面。

intro.en: Bit is a base noun, so the items below are its inflection, the phrases it appears in and the parts of its compounds.
intro.cn: bit 是基础名词，下面列出的是它的屈折形式、它出现的短语以及复合词的组成部分。

latinIntro.en: Latin morsus and frustum are recorded words for a bite and a piece; they are parallels, not the source of bit.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 morsus 与 frustum 分别是有记录的「咬」与「一块」，它们是平行词，不是 bit 的来源。

items.example: Bita is the recorded source of bit.
items.exampleCN: bita 是 bit 有记录的来源。
它把 bit 变成 bits。

items.example: It forms a bit of bread.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 a bit of bread。

definition_zh: 隐藏；把……藏起来；隐瞒；躲藏
definition_en: to put something where it cannot be seen, or to keep a fact secret
core_image: 把东西塞进看不见的角落
scene: 考试前弟弟把漫画书压在枕头下，怕被妈妈收走。 He decided to hide the comic book under his pillow before his mother came in.
sceneCN: 这里 hide 是「藏起来」（第 1 个义项：放置使不被看见）；弟弟把漫画书压在枕头下不让妈妈发现。

derivatives.zh: 由过去分词转形容词，义为「隐藏的；秘密的」
由现在分词转名词，义为「躲藏（处）」
hide 加 out 构成，义为「藏身处」
hide 加 away 构成，义为「僻静的藏身地」

senses.title: To put out of sight
senses.definition: to put something in a place where it cannot be seen or found
senses.definitionCN: 把东西放到看不见或找不到的地方
senses.example: The cat hid her toys under the sofa.
senses.exampleCN: 猫把玩具藏在沙发下面。
senses.why: Out of sight means out of reach; hiding moves a thing beyond the eyes.
senses.whyCN: 看不见就够不着；藏就是把东西移出视线之外。

senses.title: To keep a fact secret
senses.definition: to keep information or feelings secret from others
senses.definitionCN: 不让别人知道某信息或某情感
senses.example: She tried to hide her disappointment about the result.
senses.exampleCN: 她尽量掩饰对结果的失望。
senses.why: Feelings and facts can be put out of sight exactly like objects.
senses.whyCN: 情感与事实可以像物品一样被移出视线。

senses.title: To go where one cannot be seen
senses.definition: to go to or stay in a place where you cannot be seen
senses.definitionCN: 到看不见自己的地方去或待在那里
senses.example: The rabbit hid in the tall grass until the hawk left.
senses.exampleCN: 兔子在高草里躲到老鹰飞走。
senses.why: A person hiding puts the body itself out of sight.
senses.whyCN: 藏起来的人把自己整个移出视线。

intro.en: Hide comes from an old Germanic root about covering and watching over.
intro.cn: hide 来自一个表示「遮盖、看护」的古日耳曼词根。

items.en: Old English hydan meant to conceal or to cover.
items.cn: 古英语 hydan 意为隐藏、遮盖。

items.en: It goes back to Proto-Germanic *hudjan, related to hud (cover).
items.cn: 它可追溯到原始日耳曼语 *hudjan，与 hud（盖）相关。

items.en: The same root gave hut, the protective covering of a body.
items.cn: 同一词根衍生出 hut，指身体的保护覆盖物。

items.en: Middle English kept hiden with both object and body senses.
items.cn: 中古英语 hiden 兼有藏物与藏身之义。

items.en: Modern English adds the sense of hiding facts and feelings.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了隐瞒事实与情感之义。

note.en: Watch the two homonyms and the near synonyms.
note.cn: 注意同音异义词与近义词。

entries.definition: a quiet secluded retreat
entries.definitionCN: 僻静的藏身地，同根复合词

entries.definition: past participle as adjective
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词转形容词「隐藏的」

entries.definition: past tense form
entries.definitionCN: 过去式形式

entries.definition: to hide deliberately
entries.definitionCN: 故意隐藏，较正式

entries.definition: to put something over or hide it
entries.definitionCN: 盖上或遮住

entries.definition: to change appearance to hide identity
entries.definitionCN: 改变外观以隐藏身份

normalIntro.en: Use the family and the game.
normalIntro.cn: 用词族和游戏记 hide。

normal.en: hide and seek is the classic hiding game.
normal.cn: hide and seek（捉迷藏）是经典的藏身游戏。

normal.en: hid, hidden: past and participle follow the pattern.
normal.cn: hid、hidden：过去式与过去分词按不规则变化记。

normal.en: hide the gift, hide the truth: things and facts both hide.
normal.cn: 藏礼物、藏真相——物与事实都能 hide。

normal.en: hideout is where you hide out.
normal.cn: hideout 就是躲藏的据点，hide 加 out 一听即懂。

normal.en: The animal noun hide shares the spelling only.
normal.cn: 名词 hide（兽皮）只与动词 hide 拼写相同，词源不同。

abstract.en: Picture a hand sweeping a toy under the blanket.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把玩具扫进毯子下——hide 的动作。

abstract.en: Feel hide as darkness closing over an object.
abstract.cn: 把 hide 感受成黑暗罩住物体的过程。

abstract.en: Imagine yourself shrinking behind a curtain.
abstract.cn: 想象自己缩到窗帘后面——藏身的画面。

examples.en: The children played hide and seek in the garden.
examples.cn: 孩子们在花园里玩捉迷藏。

examples.en: He could not hide his excitement about the trip.
examples.cn: 他掩饰不住对这次旅行的兴奋。

examples.en: The password was hidden in the poem.
examples.cn: 密码藏在那首诗里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「害得」——「害得我只好躲起来」，躲藏正是 hide。

root: hide 来自古英语 hydan（隐藏），源自原始日耳曼语 *hudjan（遮盖），与 hut（兽皮，作覆盖物）同源。动词 hide（藏）与名词 hide（兽皮）同形但词源不同。

sensesIntro.en: From hiding things to hiding facts to hiding yourself, one idea of leaving the visible world.
sensesIntro.cn: hide 从藏物、瞒事到藏身，核心都是「离开可见的世界」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: moving something out of every eye's reach
core.cn: 核心意象：把某物移出所有眼睛的可达范围

branches.en: putting an object out of sight
branches.cn: 把物品藏到看不见处（义项 01）

branches.en: keeping facts or feelings secret
branches.cn: 让事实或情感保密（义项 02）

branches.en: placing your body out of view
branches.cn: 把自己藏到视线外（义项 03）

branches.en: disappearing from view
branches.cn: 从视野中消失（义项 01 · 03）

branches.en: a mask over the truth
branches.cn: 罩住真相的面具（义项 02）

intro.en: Hide builds a compact family of hiding places and states.
intro.cn: hide 构建出一组表示藏身处所与状态的小词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin con- (together, wholly) strengthens conceal.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语前缀 con-（完全）强化 conceal。

items.meaning: put or kept out of sight
items.example: The room held a hidden door.

items.meaning: the act or place of hiding
items.example: The fox went to its hiding place.
They built a small hideaway in the woods.
items.exampleCN: 他们在林中建了个隐蔽小屋。

items.example: He concealed his address from everyone.
items.exampleCN: 他对所有人隐瞒了住址。

items.meaning: animal skin; old sense of covering
items.example: The bag is made of cow hide.
Cover the pot with a lid.
He wore glasses as a disguise.

definition_zh: 极小的；微小的；细小的；微不足道的
definition_en: extremely small in size, amount, or importance
core_image: 掌心上一粒几乎看不见的小沙，得眯起眼才分得清
scene: 雨后的石阶上，一只小生物正慢慢横着爬。 A tiny crab crossed the wet step and disappeared into a crack.
sceneCN: 这里 tiny 是「极小的」（第 1 个义项：体积非常小）；句意为一只极小的蟹爬过湿石阶，钻进石缝不见了。画面有水光、石阶与一条细缝。

pos.zh: 形容词：极小的；微小的；细小的

derivatives.zh: 加 -ness 构成，义为「微小；极小」
形容词比较级，义为「更小的」
形容词最高级，义为「最小的」

senses.title: Extremely small in size
senses.definition: very small indeed in physical size
senses.definitionCN: 体积确实非常小
senses.example: A tiny insect landed on the page.
senses.exampleCN: 一只极小的虫子落在书页上。
senses.why: The word is probably a northern form related to little, with the ending shaping a diminutive.
senses.whyCN: 本词很可能是与 little 相关的北方方言形式，词尾带有「小」的意味。

senses.title: Small in amount
senses.definition: very small in quantity or degree
senses.definitionCN: 数量或程度上非常小
senses.example: Only a tiny amount of salt is needed.
senses.exampleCN: 只需要极少一点盐。
senses.why: The size sense transfers to quantity: a small amount is measured on the same scale as a small object.
senses.whyCN: 大小义转到数量上：少量与小的物体用同一把尺子衡量。

senses.title: Small and endearing
senses.definition: small in a way that makes people fond
senses.definitionCN: 小得让人心生喜爱
senses.example: She bought a tiny pair of boots for the doll.
senses.exampleCN: 她给娃娃买了一双小小的靴子。
senses.why: Smallness plus care gives the affectionate tone the word often carries.
senses.whyCN: 细小的体积配上用心，本词常带着亲昵的口气。

senses.title: Small in importance
senses.definition: of very little importance or significance
senses.definitionCN: 重要性或意义很小
senses.example: The differences between the two drafts were tiny.
senses.exampleCN: 两份草稿之间的差别微乎其微。
senses.why: If physical size is near zero, importance measured the same way is also near zero.
senses.whyCN: 若体积近乎零，用同一把尺子衡量的重要性也近乎零。

senses.title: A tiny fraction
senses.definition: a very small proportion of a whole
senses.definitionCN: 整体中一个非常小的份额
senses.example: A tiny fraction of the budget went to repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 预算中极小一部分用于维修。
senses.why: A part cut small enough is described with the size word rather than a counting word.
senses.whyCN: 被切得足够小的一份，用大小词而非计数词来描述。

senses.title: The tiniest detail
senses.definition: the most minute element, in the superlative tiniest
senses.definitionCN: 最高级形式下指最细小的要素
senses.example: She noticed the tiniest change in his voice.
senses.exampleCN: 她发觉他声音里最细微的变化。
senses.why: Even a detail has a size, and at the smallest scale it becomes tiny.
senses.whyCN: 细节也有大小，到了最小尺度就成了 tiny。

senses.title: Small and young
senses.definition: used of a very young person or animal
senses.definitionCN: 形容年幼的人或动物
senses.example: The tiny kitten could not yet open its eyes.
senses.exampleCN: 那只幼小的猫还睁不开眼。
senses.why: Young bodies are small bodies, so age and size share the same word.
senses.whyCN: 幼小的身体就是小小的身体，年龄与大小共用一词。

senses.title: Small in comparison
senses.definition: small when set beside something much larger
senses.definitionCN: 与更大之物相比显得很小
senses.example: From the air the ship looked tiny.
senses.exampleCN: 从空中看去那艘船显得极小。
senses.why: The word often measures against a larger frame, making size relative rather than fixed.
senses.whyCN: 这个词常相对更大的参照来衡量，因此大小是相对的。

intro.en: The adjective appears in the late sixteenth century, probably from a northern or British dialect form related to little, with a diminutive ending.
intro.cn: 这个形容词在十六世纪末出现，很可能来自与 little 相关的地方方言形式，并带有表小的词尾。

items.en: A dialect form tine or tiney is recorded for little or small.
items.cn: 方言形式 tine、tiney 已有记载，意为「小的」。

items.en: Scholars connect it with little, but the exact path is not settled.
items.cn: 学者把它与 little 联系起来，但确切路径尚未定论。

items.en: Tiny is recorded in written English from the late sixteenth century.
items.cn: tiny 自十六世纪末见于书面英语。

items.en: The comparative tinier and the superlative tiniest stabilize by the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 比较级 tinier 与最高级 tiniest 在十八世纪定型。

items.en: The word becomes the everyday strong form of small, warmer than minute.
items.cn: 本词成为 small 的日常强形式，比 minute 更带感情。

items.en: It spreads from physical size to amount, detail, and importance.
items.cn: 它从体积扩展到数量、细节与重要性。

note.en: The look-alike group holds other words ending in a similar shape, while the near-meaning group gathers the scale of smallness.
note.cn: 形近组列出结尾形状相似的其他词，近义组则聚集「小」的程度上的一组词。

entries.definition: the quality of being extremely small
entries.definitionCN: 微小；极小

entries.definition: the most extremely small
entries.definitionCN: 最小的

entries.definition: a soft metal, a different word
entries.definitionCN: 锡；只是形近，词源不同

entries.definition: a light ringing sound, a different word
entries.definitionCN: 叮当声；只是形近，词源不同

entries.definition: extremely small, in a formal register
entries.definitionCN: 极小的；细微的

entries.definition: made as a much smaller copy
entries.definitionCN: 微型的

entries.definition: small in degree or amount
entries.definitionCN: 微小的；轻微的

entries.definition: extremely large
entries.definitionCN: 巨大的

normalIntro.en: These memories work from the word's dialect origins, its scale, and the comparisons it invites.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条从它的方言来源、尺度以及它引出的对比入手。

normal.en: Tiny is probably a dialect cousin of little, so the small meaning is built in.
normal.cn: tiny 很可能是 little 的方言近亲，小的意思天生带着。

normal.en: Tinier and tiniest follow the y to i rule: y becomes i before -er.
normal.cn: tinier 与 tiniest 遵守 y 变 i 的规则。

normal.en: A tiny bit is the everyday phrase for a very small quantity.
normal.cn: a tiny bit 是表示极少量的日常说法。

normal.en: The tiniest detail uses the superlative for the finest point.
normal.cn: the tiniest detail 用最高级表示最细微之处。

normal.en: Minute is formal, tiny is warm; huge is the exact opposite.
normal.cn: minute 偏正式，tiny 更亲切，huge 正好相反。

abstract.en: Picture a pinhead with a whole insect balanced on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一根针的针头上落着一整只虫子。

abstract.en: Think of a ship seen from a plane window, no bigger than a speck.
abstract.cn: 想从机窗望见的一艘船，小得像一粒斑点。

abstract.en: A tiny thing demands that you lean closer, and leaning is the word's feeling.
abstract.cn: 微小之物逼你凑近，凑近正是这个词的感觉。

examples.en: A tiny bird was perched on the wire.
examples.cn: 一只极小的鸟停在电线上。

examples.en: Add a tiny bit of sugar to the sauce.
examples.cn: 在酱汁里加一点点糖。

examples.en: From the top of the hill the houses looked tiny.
examples.cn: 从山顶看去，那些房子显得很小。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「太迷你」——太迷你了，小得放在掌心都找不着。

root: 一般认为与 little 相关的方言形式 tiney 有关，词尾带表小色彩，确切来源不确定；十六世纪末进入书面英语。

sensesIntro.en: One scale of smallness runs through the entry: physical size first, then amount, affection, importance, fractions, details, young creatures, and size seen from far away.
sensesIntro.cn: 一条「小」的尺度贯穿全词：先体积，再到数量、亲昵、重要性、比例、细节、幼小以及远观的大小。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a speck on the palm that you must squint to see.
core.cn: 核心意象：掌心一粒得眯眼才看得见的尘点。

branches.en: Small bodies, including young ones.
branches.cn: 小的身体，包括幼小的个体。

branches.en: Smallness measured in quantity and proportion.
branches.cn: 以数量与比例衡量的小。

branches.en: The affectionate colour of the size.
branches.cn: 体积带来的亲昵色彩。

branches.en: Smallness of importance and of detail.
branches.cn: 重要性与细节上的微小。

branches.en: Small compared with a larger frame.
branches.cn: 与更大参照相比显出的小。

intro.en: The adjective takes the regular English endings for comparison and a noun, plus the y to i spelling change.
intro.cn: 这个形容词接常规英语的比较级与名词词尾，并遵守 y 变 i 的拼写规则。

latinIntro.en: Tiny has no Latin etymon; the Latin items below offer the formal scale of smallness for comparison.
latinIntro.cn: tiny 没有拉丁词源；下面的拉丁词提供正式语体的「小」尺度作对照。

items.example: The ending gives tiny its adjective shape.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾让 tiny 成为形容词。

items.meaning: y becomes i before a suffix
items.meaningCN: 后缀前 y 变 i
items.example: Tiniest drops the y for i.
items.exampleCN: tiniest 把 y 换成 i。

items.example: Tinish is not standard but would mean somewhat small.
items.exampleCN: tinish 不属标准词，但意为「有点小」。
tiny 没有常用副词形式。

items.example: Semi-tiny is only a playful formation.

definition_zh: 分开；划分；分配；使产生分歧；分界线
definition_en: to separate into parts, or to share out among people
core_image: 一刀把整块蛋糕分成两半
scene: 烘焙课后，老师端出烤好的蛋糕，用长刀从中间划下去。 Let us divide the cake into eight equal pieces.
sceneCN: 这里 divide 是「分开、划分」（第 1 个义项：把整体分成若干部分）；句意：我们把蛋糕分成八等份。

derivatives.zh: divide 加名词后缀构成，义为「分开；部门；除法」
division 加形容词后缀构成，义为「引起分裂的」
与 divide 同根的词，义为「被除数；股息」
sub- 加 divide 构成，义为「再分；细分」

senses.title: Separate into parts
senses.definition: to cut or split a whole into pieces
senses.definitionCN: 把整体切开或分成若干块
senses.example: Divide the paper into four squares.
senses.exampleCN: 把纸分成四个方格。
senses.why: Latin dividere means to force apart: a whole is pushed into separate pieces by a line or cut.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 dividere 意为「用力分开」：整体被一条线或一刀推成独立的块。

senses.title: Share out among people
senses.definition: to give out portions of something to several people
senses.definitionCN: 把某物分成几份发给众人
senses.example: The children divided the sweets among themselves.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们把糖果分了。
senses.why: Separating is the first step of sharing: each person receives one divided part.
senses.whyCN: 分开是分配的第一步：每人拿到分出的一份。

senses.title: Mathematics: find how many times
senses.definition: to find how many times one number contains another
senses.definitionCN: 求一个数包含另一个数多少次
senses.example: Divide twelve by three and you get four.
senses.exampleCN: 十二除以三等于四。
senses.why: The operation repeatedly takes parts out of a total, so the word for splitting fits it.
senses.whyCN: 这个运算反复从一个总数里取份，所以「分开」一词正好贴合。

senses.title: Cause disagreement
senses.definition: to make people form opposing groups
senses.definitionCN: 使人们形成对立的群体
senses.example: The plan divided the village into two camps.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方案让村民分成两派。
senses.why: A line that cuts a cake can also cut a crowd: people end up on different sides.
senses.whyCN: 切蛋糕的那条线也能切开人群：人们站到了两边。

senses.title: A dividing line or boundary
senses.definition: a line that separates two areas or groups
senses.definitionCN: 分隔两个区域或群体的线
senses.example: The river is the divide between the two farms.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河是两个农场的分界线。
senses.why: The act of separating freezes into the line that does the separating.
senses.whyCN: 分开的动作凝固成那条执行分开的线。

intro.en: Divide comes from a Latin verb about forcing things apart, and that cut still runs through sharing, sums and quarrels.
intro.cn: divide 来自一个拉丁动词，本义是用力分开；这道切口贯穿了分配、算术与争执。

items.en: Latin dividere meant to force apart, to split, related to vidua, a thing cut off.
items.cn: 拉丁语 dividere 意为「用力分开、劈开」，与 vidua（被切下的部分）同族。

items.en: The root appears in the motto divide and rule, dividing peoples to govern them.
items.cn: 词根见于格言 divide and rule（分而治之），即分化民众以便统治。

items.en: Old French diviser carried the sense of splitting and sharing out.
items.cn: 古法语 diviser 承载了劈开与分配的意思。

items.en: English took divide in the fourteenth century for separating wholes into parts.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语借入 divide，指把整体分成部分。

items.en: The word now names the maths operation and social splits as well.
items.cn: 如今这个词也指数学中的除法运算与社会分裂。

note.en: These words stand near divide in form or meaning.
note.cn: 这些词在形式或意义上与 divide 相邻。

normal.cn: divide into 是基本搭配：divide it into two（分成两份）。

normal.cn: division 是名词，也连着除法的概念。

normal.cn: subdivide 指再细分。

normal.en: The great divide names both watersheds and quarrels.
normal.cn: a great divide 既指分水岭也指大分歧。

normal.en: Divide the sweets shows sharing after cutting.

abstract.cn: 看那道刀线笔直穿过正中。

abstract.cn: 感受两半缓缓分开。

abstract.en: Hear classmates arguing on either side of the line.

examples.en: The teacher divided the class into four groups.
examples.cn: 老师把全班分成四个小组。

examples.en: They divided the profits equally among the partners.
examples.cn: 他们把利润平均分给合伙人。

examples.en: A narrow path divides our garden from theirs.
examples.cn: 一条小径把我家花园与他们家的隔开。

definition_zh: 数字；图表；人物；身材；轮廓；认为；理解（figure out）
definition_en: a number, the shape of a body, a person of note, or a diagram; as a verb, to calculate or to understand something
core_image: 黑板上一串数字连成图案，图案又勾勒出一个人的轮廓
scene: 会计部灯还亮着，员工核对年底的账目。 She stayed late to figure out where the totals had gone wrong.
sceneCN: 这里 figure 是动词，指「想出、弄明白」，对应第 6 个义项；句意为她加班到很晚，弄清总数错在哪里。

pos.zh: 数字；图表；人物；身材；轮廓

比喻地；象征性地（figurative 加副词后缀 -ly）

senses.title: A number, especially in records
senses.definition: a number, especially one shown in statistics or accounts
senses.definitionCN: 数字，尤指统计或账目中的数值
senses.example: The sales figures surprised everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 销售数字令所有人大吃一惊。
senses.why: Written marks that carry quantity are figures: the ink itself shows shape.
senses.whyCN: 承载数量的书写符号即 figures：墨迹本身就显示形状。

senses.title: The shape of a body
senses.definition: the shape of a person's body
senses.definitionCN: 人身体的形状
senses.example: She keeps her figure by swimming.
senses.exampleCN: 她靠游泳保持身材。
senses.why: The outer form of a person is the shape their life is drawn in.
senses.whyCN: 人的外形是生命被勾画出的轮廓。

senses.title: A person seen as a shape or name
senses.definition: a person, especially one important or well known
senses.definitionCN: 一个人，尤指重要或知名的人
senses.example: He became a key figure in the reform.
senses.exampleCN: 他成了改革中的关键人物。
senses.why: From afar, people are shapes moving in history: figures on a stage.
senses.whyCN: 远观时，人是历史中移动的剪影：舞台上的 figure。

senses.title: A diagram or drawing
senses.definition: a drawing or diagram in a book to explain something
senses.definitionCN: 书中用于说明事物的图示
senses.example: See figure 3 for the wiring diagram.
senses.exampleCN: 接线图见图 3。
senses.why: A picture fixed the meaning before words could: figure as diagram.
senses.whyCN: 在言语之前，图画先固定了含义：figure 即图示。

senses.title: To calculate a number
senses.definition: to work out an amount with numbers
senses.definitionCN: 用数字算出一个金额或数量
senses.example: We figured the cost at two thousand.
senses.exampleCN: 我们估算成本为两千。
senses.why: Moving shapes and numbers about in the mind is how arithmetic feels.
senses.whyCN: 在脑中搬运数字与形状，正是算术的体验。

senses.title: To understand after thinking
senses.definition: to understand or find an answer by thinking
senses.definitionCN: 通过思考理解或找到答案
senses.example: He figured out why the engine stalled.
senses.exampleCN: 他弄明白了引擎熄火的原因。
senses.why: Give the shapes time to settle and the answer takes form.
senses.whyCN: 让那些形状在脑中沉淀，答案便成形。

intro.en: Figure comes from Latin figura 'shape, form', from fingere 'to shape', and keeps both the drawn outline and the formed idea.
intro.cn: figure 源自拉丁语 figura「形状、形态」，出自 fingere「塑造」，同时保留「勾画的轮廓」与「成形的观念」。

items.en: Fingere meant 'to shape, mould'; its noun figura meant 'a shape or form'.
items.cn: fingere 意为「塑造、模制」；其名词 figura 意为「形状、形态」。

items.en: Old French figure carried the shape sense into Romance speech.
items.cn: 古法语 figure 把形状义带入罗曼语。

items.en: Middle English borrowed figure for body form, diagrams and numerals.
items.cn: 中古英语借入 figure，指体形、图示与数字。

items.en: The verb grew: to figure meant to calculate, then to reason out.
items.cn: 现代英语发展出动词义：先表计算，后表推理明白。

items.en: Figure out became the everyday phrase for solving problems.
items.cn: figure out 成为日常表达「解决问题」的固定说法。

note.en: Look-alikes share the fig- shape; near-meaning words cover shapes, numbers and understanding.
note.cn: 形近组共享 fig- 字形；近义组覆盖形状、数字与理解。

normal.cn: figure out 是解决问题必用的短语。

examples.en: A tall figure stood at the end of the pier.

definition_zh: 逐渐地；逐步地；缓慢地；不知不觉地
definition_en: in small steps over a period of time, rather than suddenly or all at once
core_image: 一条折线每走一小格才抬高一丝，从不直冲向上
scene: 雨停之后，浑浊的水面一点一点变清，泥沙缓缓沉到了底下。 The water gradually cleared as the sediment settled to the bottom.
sceneCN: 这里 gradually 是「逐渐地」（第 1 个义项：随时间分小步变化）；句意：随着泥沙沉到水底，水逐渐变清了。图中可辨识物件：沉降的泥沙、由浑到清的水柱、时间轴、取样瓶、缓慢下降的箭头。

pos.zh: 逐渐地；逐步地；缓慢地；不知不觉地（修饰动词、形容词或整句，位置较灵活）

derivatives.zh: 逐渐的；平缓的
渐进性
等级；坡度（同出 gradus）
梯度；坡度

senses.title: Little by little
senses.titleCN: 逐渐地：一点一点地发生
senses.definition: in small amounts over time, so that the change is felt only after a while
senses.definitionCN: 随时间以小量发生，要过一段时间才被察觉
senses.example: The cough gradually disappeared over three weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 咳嗽在三周内逐渐消失了。
senses.why: gradually is the adverb of gradual, from Latin gradus 'step'; each moment adds one small step.
senses.whyCN: gradually 是 gradual 的副词，出自拉丁 gradus“步”；每一刻只加一小步。

senses.title: Stage by stage
senses.titleCN: 逐步地：按阶段依次推进
senses.definition: stage by stage, following a planned sequence
senses.definitionCN: 按计划好的次序逐阶段进行
senses.example: The old equipment was gradually replaced over four years.
senses.exampleCN: 旧设备在四年间被逐步更换。
senses.why: The adverb can mark deliberate phasing as well as natural drift; the staircase is the same, only the builder differs.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词既可标记自然漂移，也可标记有意分批；阶梯相同，只是建造者不同。

senses.title: Without being noticed
senses.titleCN: 不知不觉地：变化小到没人留意
senses.definition: so slowly that those involved do not notice the change as it happens
senses.definitionCN: 缓慢到当事者在变化发生时都未察觉
senses.example: The town gradually lost its young people without anyone planning it.
senses.exampleCN: 这座小镇在无人规划的情况下不知不觉失去了年轻人。
senses.why: Small steps fall below attention; the adverb often carries this 'we only saw it afterwards' flavour.
senses.whyCN: 小步小到落在注意力之下；这个副词常带“事后才发现”的意味。

senses.title: At a slow rate
senses.definition: at a low speed, with intervals between the changes
senses.definitionCN: 以很低的速度，变化之间有明显间隔
senses.example: The glacier moves gradually, a few centimetres a day.
senses.exampleCN: 冰川缓慢移动，一天只有几厘米。
senses.why: Gradual change need not be deliberate; the adverb also simply reports a low rate of movement.
senses.whyCN: 渐进变化未必是有意的；这个副词也可以只报告很低的运动速率。

senses.title: By measured reform
senses.titleCN: 渐进式地：改革上一小步一小步走
senses.definition: by measured, incremental reform rather than by a single decisive change
senses.definitionCN: 以有节制、增量的改革方式，而非一次决定性变革
senses.example: The rules were gradually relaxed rather than abolished.
senses.exampleCN: 这些规定是被逐步放宽的，而不是被废除的。
senses.why: Policy adverbs signal pace; gradually here contrasts with overnight repeal.
senses.whyCN: 政策类副词标示节奏；此处的 gradually 与“一夜废除”相对。

senses.title: Accumulating in effect
senses.titleCN: 一点点累积地：效果叠加起来
senses.definition: in a way whose effects add up until they become large
senses.definitionCN: 以下述方式：效果不断叠加，直到变得显著
senses.example: Years of sediment gradually raised the river bed.
senses.exampleCN: 多年泥沙一点点抬高了河床。
senses.why: Many tiny increments can total a great change, which is why gradual processes surprise people with their final scale.
senses.whyCN: 许多微小增量可以累成巨大变化，这正是渐进过程常以其最终规模令人吃惊的原因。

senses.title: Easing off in slope
senses.titleCN: 平缓地：坡度一点点变化
senses.definition: of terrain or a curve, changing height with a gentle gradient
senses.definitionCN: 指地形或曲线以平缓的梯度改变高度
senses.example: The ridge gradually falls away towards the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 山脊朝大海方向平缓地降下去。
senses.why: The same staircase image applies to ground: each metre drops only a little.
senses.whyCN: 同一阶梯意象也适用于地面：每走一米只下降一点点。

senses.title: Turning into something else
senses.titleCN: 渐渐转为：状态慢慢过渡
senses.definition: used before verbs of becoming to show a slow transition from one state to another
senses.definitionCN: 用于“变得”类动词前，表示从一种状态缓慢过渡到另一种
senses.example: The debate gradually became a quarrel.
senses.exampleCN: 这场辩论渐渐变成了一场争吵。
senses.why: Transitions are where gradual is most useful: the adverb marks that no single moment separates the two states.
senses.whyCN: 过渡正是 gradual 最有用之处：这个副词标记没有任何单一时刻把两种状态分开。

intro.en: Gradually is the English adjective gradual plus the adverb ending -ly, from Old English -līce. The root is Latin gradus 'step'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: gradually 是英语形容词 gradual 加副词词尾 -ly（源自古英语 -līce）。词根为拉丁 gradus“步”。年代为约数。

items.en: gradus 'step, rank' came from gradi 'to walk'. The family reached English through French and directly from Latin at different periods.
items.cn: gradus“步、等级”出自 gradi“行走”。这一词族在不同时期经法语以及直接从拉丁语进入英语。

items.en: gradual is recorded in the 15th century with the sense 'step by step'. Its -al ending marks a Latin-derived adjective.
items.cn: gradual 于 15 世纪有记录，意为“一步一步地”。其 -al 词尾标记拉丁来源形容词。

items.en: -ly goes back to Old English -līce, originally a separate word meaning 'body, form'. It became the standard adverb ending and attached to Latin-derived adjectives without difficulty.
items.cn: -ly 可追溯到古英语 -līce，原为意为“身体、形态”的独立词，后成为标准副词词尾，并毫无困难地附着在拉丁来源形容词上。

items.en: Gradually became the usual adverb of slow change in ordinary prose, while the adjective remained more formal and often attributive.
items.cn: gradually 成为普通书面语中表示缓慢变化的常用副词，而形容词 gradual 更正式，且多作定语。

items.en: The exact first record of gradually is uncertain, and the deeper Indo-European root behind gradi is reconstructed, not attested.
items.cn: gradually 的确切首见记录存疑；gradi 背后的更深印欧词根属重构，并无实际记录。

note.en: The first group contains words easily mistaken for this adverb; the second contains adverbs of slow or staged change.
note.cn: 第一组是易被误认作本副词的词；第二组是表示缓慢或分阶段变化的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective. Use it after a linking verb or before a noun; use gradually to modify an action verb.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词；跟在系动词后或置于名词前；修饰动作动词时应使用 gradually。

entries.definition: Not an English word; it is a common misspelling produced by blending gradual and gradually.
entries.definitionCN: 并非英语词，是把 gradual 与 gradually 混写而成的常见错拼。

entries.definition: Continuous and not changing suddenly, as in a steady increase.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「稳定的；持续的」，如稳定增长，与 gradually 的渐进义相关。

entries.definition: From grave 'serious', meaning 'seriously'. It sounds close but comes from a different Latin word.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 grave“严重的”，意为“严重地”；读音接近，但来源是另一个拉丁词。

entries.definition: At a low speed; it says nothing about small steps or stages.
entries.definitionCN: 以低速度；不涉及小步或阶段。

entries.definition: Stage by stage and usually with a direction of advance; often slightly approving.
entries.definitionCN: 逐阶段推进，通常带前进方向，常略含褒义。

entries.definition: By small added amounts; technical and neutral about time.
entries.definitionCN: 以小额增量；偏技术，对时间中性。

entries.definition: At a constant rate; the pace may be fast as long as it does not vary.
entries.definitionCN: 以恒定速率；只要节奏不变，速度可以很快。

entries.definition: So slightly that it cannot be perceived; it sharpens sense 3 but implies even smaller steps.
entries.definitionCN: 轻微到无法察觉；强化第 3 个义项，但暗示步子更小。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: gradual + -ly: the adverb form of 'step by step'.
normal.cn: gradual + -ly：“一步一步”的副词形式。

normal.en: gradually increase, gradually decline and gradually become are the standard frames.
normal.cn: gradually increase、gradually decline、gradually become 是标准框架。

normal.en: Four syllables: gra-DU-al-ly, with no 'cal' sound in it.
normal.cn: 四个音节：gra-DU-al-ly，其中没有“cal”的音。

normal.en: Use gradually with action verbs and gradual with nouns: the price rose gradually; a gradual rise.
normal.cn: 动作动词配 gradually，名词配 gradual：价格逐渐上涨；一次逐渐的上涨。

normal.en: The family is gradual, gradually, gradualness, grade, gradient and graduate.
normal.cn: 同族词是 gradual、gradually、gradualness、grade、gradient、graduate。

abstract.en: Picture a thermometer rising one notch at a time, never jumping.
abstract.cn: 想象温度计一格一格上升，从不跳跃。

abstract.en: Picture a photograph taken once a year for fifty years, each frame almost the same as the last.
abstract.cn: 想象五十年里每年拍一张照片，每一帧都与上一帧几乎相同。

abstract.en: Picture a stone stair worn down by feet, one shallow dip added each century.
abstract.cn: 想象一级石阶被脚步磨低，每个世纪只多出一道浅坑。

examples.en: The noise gradually faded as the train moved away.
examples.cn: 随着火车远去，噪音逐渐消失了。

examples.en: Scientists gradually came to accept that the climate had shifted.
examples.cn: 科学家们渐渐接受了气候已经改变这一事实。

examples.en: The path climbs gradually for the first kilometre, then turns steep.
examples.cn: 小路在第一公里平缓上升，然后变陡。

dict_mnemonic.text: “格（gra）拉（dual）一下，慢慢走”——一格一格地前进 → gradually 逐渐地

root: 拉丁 gradus“步”+ -alis → 英语 gradual + -ly（古英语 -līce 副词词尾）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses are one adverb doing one job: marking change that arrives in small steps, whether in time, in policy, in slope or in a state of mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项是同一个副词在做一件事：标记以小步到来的变化，无论这变化在时间、政策、坡度还是心境上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line that rises by tiny increments and never jumps.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条以小增量上升、从不跳跃的线。

branches.en: ACCUMULATION: tiny steps add up, and the adverb covers both the adding and the final size.
branches.cn: 累积：微小步子叠加起来，这个副词既覆盖叠加过程，也覆盖最终规模。

branches.en: DESIGNED PACE: staged replacement and stepwise reform give the staircase a planner.
branches.cn: 设计节奏：分批更换与逐步改革为这条阶梯安排了设计者。

branches.en: BELOW ATTENTION: steps small enough to escape notice are the adverb's most characteristic effect.
branches.cn: 低于注意力：小到不被察觉的步子，是这个副词最典型的效应。

branches.en: RATE AND GROUND: low speed and gentle gradient are the same measure applied to motion and terrain.
branches.cn: 速率与地面：低速与缓坡是同一尺度分别用于运动与地形。

branches.en: TRANSITION: before verbs of becoming, the adverb marks a slow crossing between two states.
branches.cn: 过渡：在“变得”类动词前，这个副词标记两种状态之间的缓慢跨越。

intro.en: Gradually is gradual plus -ly, the standard English adverb ending. The Latin root grad- carries the 'step' image.
intro.cn: gradually 是 gradual 加 -ly，即标准英语副词词尾。拉丁词根 grad- 承载“步”的意象。

latinIntro.en: The grad- family spreads across English verbs and nouns: grade, gradient, gradual, graduate, degrade, upgrade and retrograde.
latinIntro.cn: grad- 词族遍布英语动词与名词：grade、gradient、gradual、graduate、degrade、upgrade、retrograde。

items.example: The fog gradually lifted from the valley.
A gradual change is easy to miss.
items.exampleCN: 渐进的变化容易被忽略。

items.example: The gradualness of the rise surprised the engineers.
items.exampleCN: 上升之缓慢让工程师们吃惊。

items.example: The train slowed on the long grade.
The pressure gradient pushes air inland.
items.exampleCN: 气压梯度把空气推向内陆。

items.meaning: to move up through the degrees of study
items.example: He graduated with a degree in geology.
items.exampleCN: 他毕业并取得地质学学位。

items.meaning: to step down in rank or quality
to step up to a higher grade
items.example: The lab upgraded its microscope last year.
items.exampleCN: 实验室去年升级了显微镜。

latinEntries.meaning: to walk, to proceed step by step
relating to, of the nature of

definition_zh: 教授；（大学的）教师；公开宣称者
definition_en: a senior teacher at a university, holding a chair or a high academic post, or a title used for such a person
core_image: 一位头发花白的学者站在讲台后，把一门学问当众讲给满堂学生
scene: 阶梯教室里坐满学生，讲台后的老人先把当天的争论讲清楚，再让学生自己反驳。 The professor spent the first ten minutes answering questions about the reading.
sceneCN: 这里表示「大学教授」（第 1 个义项：在大学里拥有教席或高级学术职位的教师）；句意为教授用开头十分钟回答关于阅读材料的问题。

pos.zh: 教授；大学教师；公开宣称者

derivatives.zh: 由 professor 加 -ial 构成，义为「教授的；有教授派头的」
由 professor 加 -ship 构成，义为「教授职位」
由 professor 加 -iate 构成，义为「教授群体；教授职位」

senses.title: A senior university teacher with a chair or high post
senses.definition: a university teacher of the highest rank, usually holding a chair in a subject
senses.definitionCN: 大学中等级最高的教师，通常在某学科拥有教席
senses.example: She was made a professor at thirty-five.
senses.exampleCN: 她三十五岁时被聘为教授。
senses.why: The Latin word was simply a person who declares publicly; the medieval university gave that declarer a fixed place and rank, and the title followed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词本只是「公开发言的人」；中世纪的大学给这种公开讲授者固定的位置与等级，教授这一头衔便由此而来。

senses.title: A title placed before a name
senses.definition: a title used before the name of someone who holds such a post
senses.definitionCN: 用在拥有该职位者姓名之前的称呼
senses.example: Professor Lane will see you now.
senses.exampleCN: 莱恩教授现在可以见你了。
senses.why: Once the post became recognised, the name of the post turned into a form of address, shortened in speech but kept whole in writing.
senses.whyCN: 职位一旦被公认，职位的名称就变成了对人的称呼；口语里常简化，书面里仍写全。

senses.title: Any teacher at an American college
senses.definition: in American usage, a teacher at a college or university of any rank
senses.definitionCN: 在美式用法中，指学院或大学里任何级别的教师
senses.example: My professor assigned two chapters for Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 我的老师布置了周五要读的两章。
senses.why: American campuses applied the grand title to ordinary instructors, so the word widened from the chair-holder to almost anyone who teaches there.
senses.whyCN: 美国校园把这一显赫头衔套在普通讲师身上，于是词义从「拥有教席者」扩大到几乎所有在那里教书的人。

senses.title: A person who declares a belief publicly
senses.titleCN: 公开宣称者；信仰表白者
senses.definition: a person who makes an open declaration, especially of religious faith
senses.definitionCN: 公开做出声明的人，尤指公开表白宗教信仰者
senses.example: The early professors of the faith met in secret.
senses.exampleCN: 早期公开表白信仰的人秘密聚会。
senses.why: This is the literal Latin sense, still visible in the word's shape: the professor is the one who professes.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁语的字面义，今天仍能从词的构造看出来：professor 就是「做公开声明的那个人」。

intro.en: Professor and profession share one Latin verb: profession names the declared work, while professor names the person who declares it.
intro.cn: professor 与 profession 共用一个拉丁动词：profession 指被声明的工作，professor 则指做声明的人。

items.en: Fateri meant to confess or acknowledge, to say openly something about oneself.
items.cn: fateri 意为承认、供认，即公开说出关于自己的事。

items.en: With pro-, the verb became profiteri, to declare publicly, whether a belief or a calling.
items.cn: 加上前缀 pro-，动词成为 profiteri，意为公开声明，对象可以是信仰，也可以是志业。

items.en: Professor was the agent noun: the person who professes, who declares openly, often a teacher of a doctrine.
items.cn: professor 是施动名词：做公开声明的人，常指某学说的讲授者。

items.en: In the medieval university a professor was one who publicly taught and disputed, and the word became tied to a teaching post.
items.cn: 在中世纪大学里，professor 指公开讲授并参与论辩的人，这个词遂与教职绑定。

items.en: English kept the academic sense as the main one, widened it in America to any college teacher, and let the religious sense fade.
items.cn: 英语以学术义为主，又在美国用法中扩大到任何大学教师，宗教义则逐渐淡去。

note.en: The first group is the same Latin family, including the noun for the declared work; the second gathers words for people who teach.
note.cn: 第一组是同一拉丁词族，包括指「被声明的工作」的那个名词；第二组收表示教书育人之人的词。

entries.definition: To declare openly that one holds a belief or does a kind of work.
entries.definitionCN: 公开声明自己持某种信念或从事某种工作。

entries.definition: The declared work or calling, rather than the person who declares it.
entries.definitionCN: 被公开认领的职业或志业，指事不指人。

entries.definition: Relating to a profession, or a person who works in one.
entries.definitionCN: 与职业有关的；从事某一职业的人。

entries.definition: A person who confesses, or a priest who hears confession.
entries.definitionCN: 忏悔者；听人告解的司铎。

entries.definition: A teacher at a university below professorial rank.
entries.definitionCN: 大学中低于教授级别的教师；讲师。

entries.definition: A person whose job is to help others learn.
entries.definitionCN: 以帮助他人学习为业的人。

entries.definition: A person who teaches or researches at a university.
entries.definitionCN: 在大学任教或做研究的人。

entries.definition: A person who studies a subject deeply.
entries.definitionCN: 深入研究某一学科的人。

normalIntro.en: The word is the agent noun of a Latin verb of public declaring, and its history runs from the street speaker to the university chair.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「公开声明」动词的施动名词，它的历史从街头的发言者一路走到大学的教席。

normal.en: Professor ends in -or, the Latin ending for the doer, so it means the one who professes.
normal.cn: professor 以 -or 结尾，这是拉丁语表示「做事者」的词尾，所以它指「做声明的人」。

normal.en: The verb behind it is profiteri, to declare openly; a professor is literally a public declarer.
normal.cn: 背后的动词是 profiteri，意为公开声明；professor 字面上就是「公开声明者」。

normal.en: Profession is the declared work, professor the declarer, so the two words split one idea into thing and person.
normal.cn: profession 是被声明的工作，professor 是声明者，两个词把同一个意思拆成了「事」与「人」。

normal.en: The academic sense grew in medieval universities, where teaching was a public act of declaring a doctrine.
normal.cn: 学术义在中世纪大学里长成，因为当时的讲课就是公开声明某种学说的行为。

normal.en: In America the title spread to all college teachers, which is why students there call any instructor professor.
normal.cn: 在美国，这一头衔扩散到所有大学教师，所以那里的学生管任何讲师都叫 professor。

abstract.en: A professor is proof that teaching was once a form of public speech, not a private exchange of notes.
abstract.cn: professor 证明教学曾经是一种公开言说，而不是私下交换笔记。

abstract.en: The same root ties the classroom to the pulpit: to profess was first to declare a faith aloud.
abstract.cn: 同一个词根把课堂与讲坛系在一起：profess 最初就是大声宣告信仰。

abstract.en: A title that once meant one who speaks in public now marks one who is allowed to be heard.
abstract.cn: 这个头衔原指在公众面前说话的人，如今标记的是「有资格被听见」的人。

examples.en: The professor answered questions for ten minutes before the lecture.
examples.cn: 教授在开讲前回答了十分钟问题。

examples.en: Professor Hall has taught chemistry here for twenty years.
examples.cn: 霍尔教授在这里教了二十年化学。

examples.en: He was appointed professor of history last autumn.
examples.cn: 他去年秋天被聘为历史学教授。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「铺若费舌」——教授在讲台上把知识铺开，费尽口舌；记住 professor 是教授。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（公开、向前）+ fateri（承认）→ profiteri（公开声明）→ professor（公开宣称者，后指公开讲授者），经中世纪大学用语进入英语；与 profession 同源，一为「声明/职业」，一为「声明者」。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the person who declares publicly; the academic post, the title before a name, the American widening and the old religious declarer all branch from that figure.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「公开做声明的人」；学术职位、姓名前的称谓、美式用法的扩大，以及旧时的宗教宣称者，都从这个人影分出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scholar behind a lectern, declaring a subject aloud to a room of listeners.
core.cn: 核心意象：一位学者站在讲台后，当众向满屋听众讲明一门学问。

branches.en: a chair-holder whose name is spoken with a title
branches.cn: 拥有教席、名字前带称谓的人

branches.en: a lecture hall filling before the first word
branches.cn: 开讲之前逐渐坐满的讲堂

branches.en: a student asking any instructor for help
branches.cn: 学生向任何一位讲师求助

branches.en: a small gathering declaring a faith in secret
branches.cn: 一小群人在暗中表白信仰

branches.en: a name card reading professor at the top
branches.cn: 名片最上方印着教授字样

intro.en: A Latin verb of public declaring, its prefix and its agent ending, plus the English endings that turn the person into a post and a quality, hold the word together.
intro.cn: 表示公开声明的拉丁动词、它的前缀与施动词尾，再加上把「人」变成职位与性质的英语词尾，共同支撑这个词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: one who professes, a public teacher
items.meaningCN: 公开宣称者；公开讲授者

definition_zh: 实验室；实验课
definition_en: a room or building with special equipment where scientific work and tests are carried out
core_image: 一排白瓷台面，玻璃器皿与滴管安静地立着
scene: 深夜的走廊只亮着一盏应急灯。 The lab on the third floor was still busy, with two students checking samples under the lamp.
sceneCN: 这里 lab 是「实验室」（第 1 个义项：配备专门设备做科学实验的房间），句意是三楼实验室仍然忙碌，两个学生在灯下检查样本。画面里有深夜走廊、应急灯与白瓷台面。

pos.zh: 名词：实验室；实验课；实验工作

derivatives.zh: lab 的完整形式，义为「实验室」
lab 与 based 合成，义为「以实验室为基础的」
lab 与 coat 合成，义为「实验服」

senses.title: A room for scientific work
senses.definition: a room or building fitted with instruments where experiments and tests are done
senses.definitionCN: 配有仪器、进行实验与检测的房间或建筑
senses.example: The samples were sent to the lab for analysis.
senses.exampleCN: 样本被送到实验室分析。
senses.why: The word is a cut-down form of laboratory, and short words suit the busy informal speech of the bench.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 laboratory 的截短形式，而简短的词正合实验台旁的日常口语。

senses.title: A practical class
senses.definition: a period of teaching in which students do practical work, often in the phrase lab session
senses.definitionCN: 学生学习实际操作的教学时段，常作 lab session
senses.example: We have a physics lab on Thursday mornings.
senses.exampleCN: 我们周四上午有物理实验课。
senses.why: Students name the timetabled session after the room where it happens, a common shift in schools.
senses.whyCN: 学生用上课的房间来命名那节课，这在校园里是常见的转指。

senses.title: A place for testing ideas
senses.definition: a setting, often outside science, where new ideas are tried out
senses.definitionCN: 常不限于科学、用于试验新想法的场所或环境
senses.example: The city became a lab for new transport schemes.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市成了新交通方案的试验场。
senses.why: A lab is a place built for testing, so any situation used to try things out borrows its name.
senses.whyCN: 实验室是为检验而设的地方，因此任何用来试新事的情境都借用它的名字。

intro.en: Lab is a shortened form of laboratory, and it became a word in its own right only in the twentieth century.
intro.cn: lab 是 laboratory 的缩略形式，作为独立词通行是二十世纪的事。

items.en: The Latin verb laborare meant to work, and laboratorium named a place for work.
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 laborare 意为「工作」，laboratorium 指干活的地方。

items.en: In alchemy the laboratorium was the room where heating and distillation were done.
items.cn: 炼金术里 laboratorium 是做加热与蒸馏的房间。

items.en: English borrowed laboratory in the seventeenth century for rooms where scientific work was done.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 laboratory，指做科学工作的房间。

items.en: The clipping lab appears in the late nineteenth century, and students and colleagues spread it.
items.cn: 缩略形式 lab 出现于十九世纪晚期，由学生与同行传开。

items.en: In the twentieth century lab also names the practical class and any place where ideas are tested.
items.cn: 二十世纪时 lab 也指实验课，以及任何试验新想法的场所。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words close in spelling; the near-meaning group gathers other places for scientific or practical work.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写接近的短词；近义组收其他科学或实践场所。

entries.definition: The full word from which lab is cut, and the more formal choice on signs.
entries.definitionCN: lab 所缩略的完整词，标牌上更正式的用字。

entries.definition: Shares the Latin work root, and means physical work or workers.
entries.definitionCN: 与之共享拉丁语「劳动」词根，指体力劳动或劳工。

entries.definition: Two letters apart, and names a rounded part of an organ.
entries.definitionCN: 差两个字母，指器官上圆钝的一部分。

entries.definition: A room with tools for making or repairing things.
entries.definitionCN: 放着工具、用来制作或修理的房间。

entries.definition: A room where an artist or a broadcaster works.
entries.definitionCN: 艺术家或播音人员工作的房间。

entries.definition: A place where patients are examined and treated.
entries.definitionCN: 检查与治疗病人的场所。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin work root, the clipping history and the collocations the word now has.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用真实的拉丁语「劳动」词根、缩略历史，以及如今的常见搭配。

normal.en: Lab is laboratory cut short, the way phone is telephone cut short.
normal.cn: lab 是 laboratory 的截短，正如 phone 是 telephone 的截短。

normal.en: Laboratory comes from Latin laborare, to work, so a lab is a workroom.
normal.cn: laboratory 出自拉丁语 laborare（工作），所以实验室就是干活的屋子。

normal.en: Lab work and lab report are the two phrases students meet first.
normal.cn: lab work 与 lab report 是学生最先遇到的两个搭配。

normal.en: A language lab teaches speech with recordings, not chemistry.
normal.cn: language lab 用录音教人说话，与化学无关。

normal.en: The plural is plain labs, with no extra change.
normal.cn: 复数是简单的 labs，没有别的变化。

abstract.en: A lab is a room built for questions: every instrument exists to take one doubt out of the world.
abstract.cn: 实验室是为问题而建的房间：每件仪器都是为消除一个疑虑而存在。

abstract.en: The word is short because work in such rooms is quick, repeated and spoken about every day.
abstract.cn: 这个词短，是因为这类房间里的工作迅速、重复、天天要提。

abstract.en: Once a lab meant a place for alchemy, now any city can be a lab for testing change.
abstract.cn: 曾经实验室是炼金之处，如今任何一座城市都可以成为试验变革的实验室。

examples.en: The water samples were tested in the lab.
examples.cn: 水样在实验室里做了检测。

examples.en: We have a chemistry lab every Tuesday.
examples.cn: 我们每周二有一次化学实验课。

examples.en: The old factory became a lab for new designs.
examples.cn: 那座旧工厂成了新设计的试验场。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来百」——来上百次实验，才得一个结果

root: 拉丁语 laborare「工作」的派生名词 laboratorium（干活之所），炼金术时代指加热致馏的房间；十七世纪英语借入 laboratory，十九世纪晚期缩略为 lab，二十世纪扩展到实验课与试验场。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: the room with instruments, the practical class held there, and any place where ideas are tried out.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：放仪器的房间，在那里上的实验课，以及任何试验新想法的地方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bench of white tiles with glassware, lamps and a notebook waiting.
core.cn: 核心意象：白瓷砖台面上摆着玻璃器皿、灯和一本待写的笔记。

branches.en: THE ROOM LINE: a space fitted out for experiment and test.
branches.cn: 房间线：为实验与检测而装配的空间。

branches.en: THE CLASS LINE: the timetabled session takes the name of the room.
branches.cn: 课程线：排定的课时借用了房间之名。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR LINE: any setting used to try new ideas becomes a lab.
branches.cn: 比喻线：任何试验新想法的情境都成了实验室。

branches.en: THE WORK LINE: the Latin root laborare makes a lab a place of work.
branches.cn: 劳动线：拉丁词根 laborare 让实验室成为干活之地。

branches.en: THE FORM LINE: a clipped word travels fast into general speech.
branches.cn: 形式线：截短的词很快走进日常语言。

intro.en: Lab is a clipping; its family is built from the full laboratory and from modern compounds.
intro.cn: lab 是截短词，其词族由完整的 laboratory 与现代合成构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin work root behind laboratory is recorded in labor and laborare.
latinIntro.cn: laboratory 背后的拉丁语「劳动」词根在 labor 与 laborare 中都有记录。

items.example: The new labs open in May.
The laboratory is on floor two.
It forms laboratory and factory-like words.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 laboratory 一类表示场所的词。

items.example: He put on a clean lab coat.
The language lab has forty seats.

items.meaningCN: 构成 lab work（实验工作）
items.example: Lab work counts for half the mark.

definition_zh: 私人的；私有的；私密的；私立的；僻静的；列兵
definition_en: belonging to one person or a small group rather than to the public; kept secret from others; not run by the state; free from other people; and, as a noun, a soldier of the lowest rank
core_image: 一扇关着的门后面，桌上摊着只给自己看的信
scene: 周末午后，小咖啡馆最里面的角落摆着一张矮桌，说话的人把声音压低，不希望邻座听见。 They chose a private corner of the coffee shop to discuss the contract.
sceneCN: 这里 private 指「私密的、不让旁人听见的」（第 2 个义项：只让少数人知道或参与的）；句意为他们挑了咖啡馆里一个私密的角落谈合同。图中可辨识物件：矮桌、压低声音的两个人、邻座的空椅。

pos.zh: 私人的；私有的；私密的；私立的；僻静的

derivatives.zh: 由 private 加名词后缀 -acy 构成，义为「隐私；私密」
由 private 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「私下地；以私人身份」
与 private 同源，出自拉丁语 privatio，义为「匮乏；剥夺」

senses.title: Belonging to one person rather than to the public
senses.definition: owned by or intended for one person or a small group, not for everyone
senses.definitionCN: 属于或专供一个人、一小群人，而不是给所有人的
senses.example: The letters are part of his private collection.
senses.exampleCN: 这些信件是他私人收藏的一部分。
senses.why: Latin privus meant single or individual, the direct opposite of publicus, so the first sense is ownership narrowed down to one person.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 privus 意为单个的、个人的，正好与 publicus 相对；所以第一层意思就是把归属缩到一个人身上。

senses.title: Kept from the knowledge of others
senses.definition: shared with only a few people and deliberately kept away from the public
senses.definitionCN: 只在少数人之间分享、有意不让公众知道的
senses.example: The meeting was private, so no notes were published.
senses.exampleCN: 那场会是不公开的，所以没有公布记录。
senses.why: What belongs to one person is also what only that person may know, so the ownership sense slides naturally into secrecy.
senses.whyCN: 属于一个人的东西，也就是只许那个人知道的东西，于是「归属」这一层自然而然地滑向「保密」。

senses.title: Not run or paid for by the state
senses.definition: owned and managed by an individual or a company rather than by the government
senses.definitionCN: 由个人或公司拥有经营，而不是由政府办的
senses.example: She moved her son from a state school to a private one.
senses.exampleCN: 她把儿子从公立学校转到了私立学校。
senses.why: When the state became the default provider of schools and hospitals, anything outside it was marked with the old word for what belongs to an individual, and this institutional sense followed.
senses.whyCN: 当国家成为学校和医院的默认提供者，凡是国家之外的就用那个表示「属于个人」的旧词来标记，这一层机构义便随之出现。

senses.title: Quiet and free from other people
senses.definition: away from crowds and public view, so that a person is not observed
senses.definitionCN: 远离人群和公众视线，人不被旁人看到
senses.example: The garden is private, and no visitors are allowed inside.
senses.exampleCN: 那座花园是私家的，访客不得入内。
senses.why: A place can be private too: if it belongs to one household, outsiders stay out, and the result is the quiet of a spot no one else enters.
senses.whyCN: 地方也可以是 private：它属于一户人家，外人就不进来，结果就是一处没人进入的安静之地。

senses.title: A soldier of the lowest rank
senses.definition: a soldier of the lowest rank, especially in the British army
senses.definitionCN: 最低军衔的士兵，尤指英国陆军中的
senses.example: He joined up as a private and retired as a sergeant.
senses.exampleCN: 他入伍时是列兵，退役时已是中士。
senses.why: The noun began as private soldier, a man serving in his own private capacity rather than as an officer, and the shorter form kept only the rank.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词起初写作 private soldier，指以个人身份服役、而非军官的人；后来缩写只留下了军衔这一层。

intro.en: Private comes from a Latin adjective meaning single or set apart, and its family keeps two faces: what belongs to one person, and what has been cut off from the rest.
intro.cn: private 出自一个意为「单个的、被分出来的」拉丁语形容词，它的词族始终保留两张面孔：属于一个人的，以及从其余部分中割出来的。

items.en: Privus meant single, individual or set apart, and it stood opposite publicus, what belongs to the people as a whole.
items.cn: privus 意为单个的、个人的、被单独分出来的，与表示「属于全体人民的」publicus 相对。

items.en: The verb privare meant to set apart or to deprive, and it supplied the idea of taking something away from the group.
items.cn: 动词 privare 意为使分离、剥夺，给出「把某物从群体中拿走」这一层意思。

items.en: Its participle privatus described a person withdrawn from public office, and from that came the sense of personal rather than official.
items.cn: 它的分词 privatus 形容退离公职的人，由此生出「属于个人而非公职」的意思。

items.en: Old French privat meant private, intimate and secret, and Middle English borrowed the word with that whole spread of meaning.
items.cn: 古法语 privat 意为私人的、亲近的、秘密的，中古英语把这一整片含义一起借了过来。

items.en: Modern English keeps the adjective for ownership, secrecy, non-state services and quiet places, while private soldier was shortened to private for the lowest rank.
items.cn: 现代英语保留形容词的四种用法：归属、保密、非国营与僻静；private soldier 则缩成 private，指最低军衔。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin stem priv- and the words English built on it; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives about what belongs to one person or is kept hidden.
note.cn: 形近组沿着拉丁词干 priv- 及英语在它上面造出的词展开；近义组收表示「属于一个人」或「被藏起来」的形容词。

entries.definition: The state of being free from public attention; built on the same stem with -acy.
entries.definitionCN: 不受公众注意的状态；同一词干加 -acy 构成。

entries.definition: In a private way, not publicly.
entries.definitionCN: 以私下的方式，非公开地。

entries.definition: The state of lacking something necessary; from Latin privatio.
entries.definitionCN: 缺少必需之物的状态；来自拉丁语 privatio。

entries.definition: To take something away from someone; built on the same Latin verb privare.
entries.definitionCN: 从某人那里拿走某物；建立在同一个拉丁动词 privare 上。

entries.definition: Relating to one particular person rather than to others.
entries.definitionCN: 与某一个特定的人有关，而非与其他人有关。

entries.definition: Kept hidden from other people.
entries.definitionCN: 对其他的人隐藏起来的。

entries.definition: Meant to be kept private between a few people.
entries.definitionCN: 只应在少数人之间保密的。

entries.definition: Single and separate, belonging to one person.
entries.definitionCN: 单个而分开的，属于一个人的。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a Latin adjective for what is single and cut off from the group, and every branch of meaning keeps either the belonging or the cutting.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在一个拉丁语形容词上，本义是「单个的、从群体里分出来的」，它的每一支意思都保留着「归属」或「切割」其中之一。

normal.en: Privus is Latin for single or individual, and it stands opposite publicus, the source of public.
normal.cn: privus 是拉丁语的「单个的、个人的」，与 publicus 相对，而 public 正出自后者。

normal.en: Privare means to set apart or deprive, which is why private and deprive share a stem.
normal.cn: privare 意为使分离、剥夺，所以 private 与 deprive 共用一个词干。

normal.en: Privacy adds -acy, the ending that turns an adjective into a state, as in accuracy.
normal.cn: privacy 加了 -acy，这个词尾把形容词变成状态，和 accuracy 一样。

normal.en: Private soldier was shortened to private, so the noun keeps only the rank, not the man.
normal.cn: private soldier 缩成了 private，于是这个名词只留下军衔，不再指那个人。

normal.en: In private is a fixed phrase: the preposition turns the adjective into an adverbial of manner.
normal.cn: in private 是固定说法，介词把这个形容词变成了方式状语。

abstract.en: The word carries both a belonging and a wall: something is mine because it is kept away from you.
abstract.cn: 这个词同时带着归属和一道墙：某物之所以是我的，正因为它被挡在你之外。

abstract.en: Public and private are the same coin struck twice, one face for the many and one for the one.
abstract.cn: public 与 private 是同一枚硬币的两面，一面给众人，一面给个人。

abstract.en: A private soldier is private in the oldest sense: a man serving as himself, not as an officer.
abstract.cn: 列兵的 private 用的是最老的那层意思：以本人身份服役，而不是以军官身份。

examples.en: The letters are part of his private collection.
examples.cn: 这些信件是他私人收藏的一部分。

examples.en: She moved her son from a state school to a private one.
examples.cn: 她把儿子从公立学校转到了私立学校。

examples.en: He joined up as a private and retired as a sergeant.
examples.cn: 他入伍时是列兵，退役时已是中士。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「普莱维特」——「不来往」的那扇门后面，才是 private 的地方。

root: 拉丁语 privus（个人的、单独的）→ privare（使分离、剥夺）→ privatus（退离公职的、私人的）→ 古法语 privat → 中古英语 privat → private。

sensesIntro.en: The core is what belongs to one person and is therefore cut off from the rest; the senses divide into ownership, secrecy, non-state service, quiet space, and the private soldier.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「属于一个人、因而与其余部分隔开」；义项由此分出归属、保密、非国营、安静的空间，以及列兵。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a closed door with a letter on the table behind it, written for one reader only.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇关着的门，门后桌上摊着一封只给一个人看的信。

branches.en: a drawer of letters with one name on it
branches.cn: 只写着一个名字的抽屉

branches.en: a door closed before a quiet conversation
branches.cn: 悄悄谈话前关上的门

branches.en: a school with its own gate and its own fees
branches.cn: 自带大门与学费的学校

branches.en: a walled garden nobody else enters
branches.cn: 别人不得进入的围墙花园

branches.en: a young soldier standing at the end of the line
branches.cn: 队列末尾站着的年轻士兵

intro.en: The word is a Latin adjective for what is single and set apart, its verb of depriving, the French form, and the English endings that name the state and the manner.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示「单个、被分出」的拉丁语形容词、表示剥夺的动词、法语词形，以及命名状态与方式的英语词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Latin privus and privare are the secure base of this family, and privatus shows how an adjective of being set apart became the ordinary word for personal.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 privus 与 privare 是这个词族可靠的根基，privatus 则展示了一个「被分开」的形容词如何变成表示「私人」的日常词。

definition_zh: 研究；调查
definition_en: careful study to discover new facts or reach a better understanding
core_image: 一个人把旧资料摊满桌子，一遍遍查找线索
scene: 为了写这篇论文，她花了半年时间查阅地方档案。 She spent six months in local archives to research the history of the town.
sceneCN: 这里 research 是「研究」（第 1 个义项：为发现事实而仔细查考）；句意：为了研究这座小镇的历史，她在地方档案馆待了半年。

derivatives.zh: 研究者；研究员
可研究的

senses.title: Systematic study of a subject
senses.definition: careful and organized study aimed at discovering facts
senses.definitionCN: 为发现事实而进行的细致、有条理的研究
senses.example: Recent research links sleep to memory.
senses.exampleCN: 最近的研究把睡眠与记忆联系起来。
senses.why: The noun names the whole activity of searching a subject again and again.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指对某个主题反复搜寻的整个活动。

senses.title: To study a subject carefully
senses.definition: to study something in detail in order to understand it
senses.definitionCN: 为理解某事物而详细研究
senses.example: She researched the history of the town for six months.
senses.exampleCN: 她研究这座小镇的历史研究了半年。
senses.why: The verb is the same repeated searching directed at a question.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是把同样的反复搜寻指向一个问题。

senses.title: Published findings
senses.definition: the results or body of work produced by study
senses.definitionCN: 研究产生的结果或成果集合
senses.example: His research on bees was published last year.
senses.exampleCN: 他关于蜜蜂的研究去年发表了。
senses.why: The activity is often named by its output, especially in academic writing.
senses.whyCN: 这项活动常以成果来指代，在学术写作中尤其如此。

intro.en: Research comes from Old French recerche, a search, from recercher, to seek out, built on re- and cerchier, to search.
intro.cn: research 来自古法语 recerche（搜寻），源于 recercher（找出），由 re- 与 cerchier（搜索）构成。

items.en: Circare means to go around or search through.
items.cn: circare 意为绕行、四处搜寻。

items.en: Cerchier means to search.
items.cn: cerchier 意为搜寻。

items.en: Recercher means to seek out thoroughly.
items.cn: recercher 意为彻底找出。

items.en: Recerche means a search or inquiry.
items.cn: recerche 意为搜寻、探究。

items.en: Middle English researchen means to investigate.
items.cn: 中古英语 researchen 意为调查、探究。

items.en: Modern English uses research for academic and scientific study.
items.cn: 现代英语中，research 用于学术与科学研究。

note.en: Research is a searching word, and it sits near its family and near words for study and inquiry.
note.cn: research 是一个「搜寻」词，与自身词族以及表示学习和探究的词相邻。

entries.definition: a person who does research
entries.definitionCN: 研究者

entries.definition: third person form of the verb
entries.definitionCN: 动词第三人称单数形式

entries.definition: past form of the verb
entries.definitionCN: 动词过去式

entries.definition: the activity of learning about a subject
entries.definitionCN: 学习；研究

entries.definition: a careful examination of facts
entries.definitionCN: 调查

entries.definition: a question or formal investigation
entries.definitionCN: 询问；调查

normalIntro.en: Research is re- plus search: to search again and again until the answer appears.
normalIntro.cn: research 是 re- 加 search：一遍又一遍地搜寻，直到答案出现。

normal.en: Re- means again, and search means look for.
normal.cn: re- 表示再一次，search 表示寻找。

normal.en: Do research is the common phrase built on the noun.
normal.cn: do research 是由名词构成的常用短语。

normal.en: Research into a subject means looking closely at it.
normal.cn: research into a subject 意为仔细考察某个主题。

normal.en: A researcher is the person who does the searching.
normal.cn: researcher 就是做搜寻工作的人。

normal.en: Compare study: study can be quiet learning, while research aims at new facts.
normal.cn: 对比 study：study 可以是安静学习，research 则旨在发现新事实。

abstract.en: Picture a table covered with open books and marked pages.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上摊满打开的书和做了标记的纸页。

abstract.en: Imagine a scientist repeating a test to be sure.
abstract.cn: 想象科学家为求确定而重复一次实验。

abstract.en: Think of a single question followed through many files.
abstract.cn: 想象一个问题被追进一摞摞档案。

examples.en: She researched the history of the town for six months.
examples.cn: 她研究这座小镇的历史研究了半年。

examples.en: Recent research links sleep to memory.
examples.cn: 最近的研究把睡眠与记忆联系起来。

examples.en: The team is doing research into clean energy.
examples.cn: 团队正在研究清洁能源。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re + search」——一遍又一遍地搜寻，就是研究；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 circare（四处搜寻）→ 古法语 cerchier（搜索）→ recercher（找出）→ recerche（探究）→ 中古英语 researchen → 现代英语 research。

sensesIntro.en: The word is a repeated search: first the activity, then the verb of studying, then the published results of that study.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词就是「反复搜寻」：先指活动，再指研究的动词，最后指研究发表的成果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a question pursued through piles of evidence.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个问题被追过成堆的证据。

branches.en: Organized study is the main noun sense.
branches.cn: 有条理的研究，是主要名词义项。

branches.en: The verb names the act of searching a subject.
branches.cn: 动词指研究某个主题的行为。

branches.en: Published findings are the visible product of research.
branches.cn: 发表成果是研究可见的产物。

branches.en: The activity and the act are two views of one effort.
branches.cn: 活动与行为是同一种努力的两个视角。

branches.en: Searching produces findings, and findings invite more searching.
branches.cn: 搜寻产生成果，成果又引来更多搜寻。

intro.en: Research is a French-shaped word built on a Latin root for searching, with English endings forming its small family.
intro.cn: research 是建立在拉丁语「搜寻」词根上的法语形态词，小词族由英语词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin circare means to go around or search, and French cerchier continues that sense.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 circare 意为绕行、搜寻，法语 cerchier 延续这一含义。

items.example: Re- adds the idea of repeating.
Cerchier carries the verb into French.
items.exampleCN: cerchier 把这个动词带入法语。

items.example: Recerche is the direct source of research.
items.exampleCN: recerche 是 research 的直接来源。

definition_zh: 消失；不见；不复存在
definition_en: to go away so that nobody can see or find it
core_image: 魔术师手中凭空消失的硬币
scene: 课间休息后，操场上的猫不见了。 The little cat disappeared behind the wall in one second.
sceneCN: 这里 disappear 是「消失」（第 1 个义项：看不见了）；句意是小猫一秒钟就消失在墙后。

derivatives.zh: disappear 的词基，义为「出现」
appear 加名词后缀构成，义为「外貌；出现」
disappear 加名词后缀构成，义为「消失」

senses.title: To go out of sight
senses.definition: to go somewhere so that people cannot see it any more
senses.definitionCN: 走到人们看不见的地方
senses.example: The sun disappeared behind the clouds.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳躲到云后面去了。
senses.why: Appear means to come into view; dis- pushes it out of view again.
senses.whyCN: appear 意为「进入视野」，dis- 又把它推出视野。

senses.title: To stop existing
senses.definition: to stop existing or being used
senses.definitionCN: 不再存在或不再被使用
senses.example: Many old customs are slowly disappearing.
senses.exampleCN: 许多古老的习俗正在慢慢消失。
senses.why: When something leaves sight forever, it leaves the world too.
senses.whyCN: 当某物永远离开视线，它也离开了这个世界。

intro.en: Disappear is appear plus the prefix dis-.
intro.cn: disappear 是 appear 加前缀 dis-。

items.en: Latin apparere meant to come forth, built on ad- (toward) and parere (to show oneself).
items.cn: 拉丁语 apparere 意为出现，由 ad-（朝向）加 parere（显露自身）构成。

items.en: Old French apareir meant to appear or to be visible.
items.cn: 古法语 apareir 意为出现、可见。

items.en: English borrowed appear in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语借入 appear。

items.en: The prefix dis- made disappear in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 十五世纪加上 dis- 构成 disappear。

items.en: Disappearance names the act; the word now also covers extinct animals and lost customs.
items.cn: disappearance 指消失这一行为；如今也用于灭绝的动物与失传的习俗。

note.en: These words share the appear root or the vanishing field.
note.cn: 这些词同出 appear 词根，或属于消失义场。

entries.definition: to come into view
entries.definitionCN: 出现

senses.whyCN: ante 意为在之前，所以这个词先标记整个位于我们之前的时代。

senses.title: Very old in itself

definition_zh: 伙伴；搭档；合伙人；配偶；与……合伙
definition_en: a person who shares an activity, a business, or a life with another; also to join with someone as a partner
core_image: 两个人各执一端，抬着同一件重物往前走
scene: 双人皮划艇上，前后两人各握一支桨。 The two paddlers must keep exactly the same rhythm, because each one is the partner of the other and the boat goes straight only when they pull together.
sceneCN: 这里 partner 是「搭档」（第 2 个义项：并肩干活的搭档）；句意：两名划手必须保持完全一致的节奏，因为彼此是对方的搭档，只有同时划桨船才会走直。图中可辨识物件：双人皮划艇、两支桨、救生衣、水面、同步的桨痕。
