senses.title: One who shares a business
senses.titleCN: 共同经营一份生意的人
senses.definition: a person who shares the ownership and risks of a business with one or more others
senses.definitionCN: 与他人共同拥有一家企业并分担风险的人
senses.example: She became a partner in the firm last year.
senses.exampleCN: 她去年成了这家事务所的合伙人。
senses.why: The oldest sense is 'one who shares'. In business the shared thing is ownership itself, so a partner is someone who holds a portion of the firm and is liable for its debts.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是“分享者”。在商业中，被分享的东西就是所有权本身，因此合伙人就是持有企业一份、并对债务负责的人。

senses.title: The one you work beside
senses.definition: a person who works with you on a task, often as an equal
senses.definitionCN: 与你共同完成一项任务的人，通常是平等的一方
senses.example: My lab partner and I split the experiments.
senses.exampleCN: 我和实验搭档分担了实验。
senses.why: Sharing can be sharing work rather than property. Two people each take one end of the task, and equality is built into the word: a partner is not a helper but a counterpart.
senses.whyCN: 分享的对象可以是工作而不是财产。两人各执任务的一端，平等就写在这个词里：partner 不是帮手，而是对等的一方。

senses.title: The one you share a life with
senses.definition: a spouse or a person with whom one lives in a committed romantic relationship
senses.definitionCN: 配偶，或与之处于稳定恋爱关系并共同生活的人
senses.example: He brought his partner to the dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 他带伴侣来参加晚宴。
senses.why: A life is the largest thing two people can share. English extended partner to the domestic sphere in the 18th century, and the word now avoids the assumptions built into husband or wife.
senses.whyCN: 生活是两个人能分享的最大一件事。英语在 18 世纪把 partner 扩展到家庭领域，如今这个词也避开了 husband 或 wife 所带的预设。

senses.title: The one across the table or on the floor
senses.titleCN: 桌对面或舞池里的搭档
senses.definition: the person matched with you in a game, dance, or performance
senses.definitionCN: 在游戏、舞蹈或表演中与你配对的人
senses.example: She danced with a new partner at the competition.
senses.exampleCN: 她在比赛中与一位新舞伴跳舞。
senses.why: A dance or a game assigns roles that only work in pairs. The partner is the other half of a required pair, which is why the word appears wherever a form demands two.
senses.whyCN: 舞蹈或游戏分配的角色只有成对才成立。partner 是某个必需配对中的另一半，因此凡是形式要求两人时，这个词就会出现。

senses.title: Partner in crime: the other half of a secret
senses.definition: a person who joins another in a mischievous or criminal activity, often used humorously
senses.definitionCN: 与他人一起干顽皮或犯罪之事的人，常作幽默用法
senses.example: The two children were partners in crime all summer.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个孩子整个夏天都是“共犯”。
senses.why: The phrase borrows the equality of partnership for something illegal. What is shared is not property but risk and secrecy, and the humorous use keeps the bond while dropping the crime.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把伙伴关系的“平等”借给了非法之事。被分享的不是财产，而是风险与秘密；幽默用法保留了这份联结，却抽掉了犯罪。

senses.title: A partner organisation or country
senses.definition: an organisation, company, or country that cooperates formally with another
senses.definitionCN: 与另一方正式合作的机构、公司或国家
senses.example: The university is a partner in the research consortium.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学是该研究联盟的合作方。
senses.why: Institutions also pair up. Here partnership is a formal relation between entities rather than between persons, but the logic is the same: each brings something and both are bound.
senses.whyCN: 机构也会结对。这里的伙伴关系是实体之间而非人与人之间的正式关系，但逻辑相同：各方都拿出东西，也都受约束。

senses.title: To partner: join as an equal
senses.titleCN: 动词：作为平等一方加入
senses.definition: to join with someone or an organisation as a partner
senses.definitionCN: 作为伙伴与某人或某机构结合
senses.example: The startup partnered with a larger manufacturer.
senses.exampleCN: 这家初创公司与一家更大的制造商结成了伙伴。
senses.why: The verb turns the relation into an act. Partnering is not hiring or assisting; it is the moment two parties agree to stand on the same level, which is why it is popular in business language.
senses.whyCN: 动词把这个关系变成动作。partnering 不是雇佣也不是帮忙，而是两方同意站在同一高度的那一刻，因此它在商业语言里很受欢迎。

senses.title: A partner in a professional firm
senses.definition: a senior member of a law or accounting firm who shares in its ownership and profits
senses.definitionCN: 律师事务所或会计师事务所中持有所有权并分享利润的高级成员
senses.example: Only partners may sign the audit report.
senses.exampleCN: 只有合伙人才能签署审计报告。
senses.why: Professional firms are owned by their senior members, so 'partner' becomes a rank as well as a relation. The title marks both ownership and the right to sign, which is why it is a career goal in law and accounting.
senses.whyCN: 专业事务所由其高级成员拥有，因此 partner 既是关系也是职级。这个头衔同时标记所有权与签署权，所以它成了法律与会计行业的一个职业目标。

intro.en: Partner began as a word for a joint heir and was reshaped by the unrelated word part. The deeper root is Latin pars, but the change from parcener to partner is not fully explained.
intro.cn: partner 最初指共同继承人，后来被另一个词 part 改形。更深词根是拉丁语 pars，但从 parcener 变成 partner 的过程并没有完整解释。

items.en: Partiner is recorded meaning 'partner, sharer'. It is an altered form of parcener 'joint heir, one who shares an inheritance'.
items.cn: partiner 记录于 1300 年前后，意为“伙伴、分享者”。它是 parcener“共同继承人、分得遗产者”的变形。

items.en: Parcener comes from Old French parçonier, from parçon 'division, share', from Latin partitionem 'a dividing', from partire 'to divide', from pars 'part'.
items.cn: parcener 来自古法语 parçonier，再上溯 parçon“分割、一份”，拉丁语 partitionem“划分”，动词 partire“分割”，以及 pars“部分”。

items.en: The -n- of parcener becomes -t-, giving partner. The change is usually attributed to the influence of part, though the exact path is source uncertain.
items.cn: parcener 中的 -n- 变成 -t-，形成 partner。这一变化通常归因于 part 的影响，但确切过程来源不确定。

items.en: The commercial sense 'one who shares in a business' is recorded. The legal and commercial senses grow together, since a partnership is both a relation and a form of ownership.
items.cn: “共同经营生意者”这一商业义记录于 16 世纪 20 年代。法律义与商业义一起成长，因为合伙既是一种关系，也是一种所有权形式。

items.en: The sense 'spouse' is recorded. Modern English extends it to any committed couple and to institutional cooperation: trading partner, partner with.
items.cn: “配偶”义记录于 1749 年。现代英语把它扩展到任何稳定的伴侣关系，也扩展到机构合作：贸易伙伴、与……合作。

note.en: The first group shares the part- root or the -er ending; the second compares words for people joined by work, trust, or love.
note.cn: 第一组共享 part- 词根或 -er 结尾；第二组比较因工作、信任或爱情而结合的人。

entries.definition: concerning only a part; biased in favour of one side. It is an adjective, not a person, and has nothing to do with partnership.
entries.definitionCN: 只涉及一部分的；偏袒一方的。它是形容词，不指人，也与合伙无关。

entries.definition: a division into parts, or a screen that divides a space. It shares the Latin pars root but names a dividing, not a sharing.
entries.definitionCN: 分成若干部分，或隔开空间的屏风。它共享拉丁语 pars 词根，但命名的是“分开”，不是“分享”。

entries.definition: a strong supporter of a party or cause. Its part is a political side, not a share held with another person.
entries.definitionCN: 某一党派或事业的坚定支持者。它的 part 指政治一方，而不是与他人共持的一份。

entries.definition: a very small piece of matter. It is a small part, with the diminutive -cle, and is not a partner.
entries.definitionCN: 极小的物质颗粒。它是“小部分”，带指小后缀 -cle，不是伙伴。

entries.definition: a person you work with, especially in a profession. It is neutral about equality and ownership, while partner implies a share.
entries.definitionCN: 与你共事的人，尤指同一专业。它对平等与所有权保持中性，而 partner 隐含“持有一份”。

entries.definition: a state or person joined with another for mutual support. It is about interests and conflict, while partner can be about work or life.
entries.definitionCN: 为相互支持而结合的国家或个人。它关乎利益与冲突，而 partner 可以关乎工作或生活。

entries.definition: a person who spends time with you. It stresses company, while partner stresses a shared role or share.
entries.definitionCN: 与你共度时光的人。它强调陪伴，而 partner 强调共同的角色或份额。

entries.definition: a husband or wife in law. It is the legal term, while partner is broader and can name an unmarried couple.
entries.definitionCN: 法律上的丈夫或妻子。它是法律术语，而 partner 更宽泛，也可指未婚伴侣。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on the sound and the shared load, then three abstract images about equality.
normalIntro.cn: 先用五个围绕读音与“共抬一物”的挂钩，再用三个关于“平等”的抽象画面。

normal.en: partner has part inside it: a partner holds a part. The spelling hides the old parcener, but the meaning kept the share.
normal.cn: partner 里面藏着 part：partner 持有一份。拼写掩盖了古老的 parcener，但词义保住了“份额”。

normal.en: Picture two people carrying one heavy box, one at each end. Neither is the boss.
normal.cn: 想两个人抬一个重箱子，各执一端。谁都不是老板。

normal.en: Business partner, dance partner, life partner: the same word slides from money to floor to home.
normal.cn: 商业合伙人、舞伴、人生伴侣：同一个词从钱滑到舞池，再滑到家。

normal.en: partner with, not partner to: the preposition marks standing alongside, not belonging to.
normal.cn: 是 partner with，不是 partner to：介词标记“并肩”，不是“附属”。

normal.en: A law firm promotes you to partner: the title means you now own a piece of the firm.
normal.cn: 律师事务所把你提升为 partner：这个头衔意味着你现在拥有事务所的一份。

abstract.en: A partner is equality made practical: two people who each hold one end and cannot move without the other.
abstract.cn: 伙伴是被实践出来的平等：两人各执一端，缺少对方就无法前进。

abstract.en: Partnership is a share in risk before it is a share in reward; that is why the word fits both marriage and business.
abstract.cn: 合伙先是风险中的一份，然后才是收益中的一份；因此这个词同时适用于婚姻与商业。

abstract.en: Calling someone a partner rather than a helper is a claim about dignity, not about workload.
abstract.cn: 称一个人为 partner 而不是 helper，是在主张尊严，而不是分配工作量。

examples.en: The two firms became partners in a joint venture.
examples.cn: 这两家公司在一次合资中成为合伙人。

examples.en: He partnered with a local charity to rebuild the school.
examples.cn: 他与当地一家慈善机构合作重建了学校。

examples.en: Her partner stayed home while she attended the conference.
examples.cn: 她去开会时，伴侣留在了家里。

dict_mnemonic.note: 把 part 记成“一份”，-ner 记成人：持有一份的人，就是合伙人、搭档、伴侣。
dict_mnemonic.text: part（一份）+ -ner（人）→ 持有一份的人 → 合伙人、搭档、伴侣

root: 古法语 parçonier < parçon“分割、一份” < 拉丁 partitionem / partire < pars“部分”；拼写受 part 影响，由 parcener 变为 partner。

sensesIntro.en: The senses go from shared ownership, to shared work, to a shared life, to a required pair in a game or dance, to a shared secret, to institutional cooperation, to the act of joining, and finally to the rank inside a professional firm.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从共同所有权，转到共担工作、共同生活、游戏或舞蹈中必需的另一半、共同保守的秘密、机构合作、结伴的动作，最后落到专业事务所内部的职级。

core.en: Two people holding one end each of the same load, walking in step
core.cn: 两人各执同一重物的一端，步调一致地前行

branches.en: Ownership: a share in a firm, and the rank that share confers.
branches.cn: 所有权：在企业中的一份，以及这份所有权带来的职级。

branches.en: The required other half: a workmate on a task, and a mate in a dance or game.
branches.cn: 必需的另一半：任务上的同事，以及舞蹈或游戏中的搭档。

branches.en: Intimacy at two temperatures: a life partner and a partner in crime.
branches.cn: 两种温度的亲密：人生伴侣与犯罪同伙。

branches.en: From persons to entities: organisations and countries as partners, still sharing risk.
branches.cn: 从人到实体：机构与国家成为伙伴，仍然共担风险。

branches.en: The verb: to join someone as an equal.
branches.cn: 动词：作为平等一方与某人结合。

intro.en: Partner's family mixes the Latin pars root with native English suffixes: the abstract partnership, the activity, the adjective, and prefixed forms.
intro.cn: partner 的词族把拉丁语 pars 词根与英语本族后缀混在一起：抽象的 partnership、活动名词、形容词，以及加前缀的形式。

latinIntro.en: The Latin chain is pars 'part' → partire 'to divide' → partitionem 'a division'. Old French parçon gave parcener, and the spelling later moved toward part.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语链条是 pars“部分”→ partire“分割”→ partitionem“划分”。古法语 parçon 给出 parcener，拼写后来又向 part 靠拢。

items.structure: altered from parcener, influenced by part

items.meaningCN: 共享生意、任务或生活的人
items.example: They have been partners for ten years.
items.exampleCN: 他们做合伙人已经十年。

items.meaning: the relation between partners; a business so owned
items.exampleCN: 这段合伙关系于 2010 年结束。

items.meaning: the act of forming a partnership
items.example: Partnering with local firms cut costs.
items.exampleCN: 与当地公司合作降低了成本。

items.meaning: having a partner; joined in a partnership
items.meaningCN: 有伴侣的；已结成伙伴的
items.example: The survey distinguishes partnered and single adults.
items.exampleCN: 该调查区分有伴侣与单身的成年人。

items.example: Each co-partner holds an equal share.
items.exampleCN: 每位共同合伙人持有相等份额。

items.example: He arrived partnerless at the dinner.
items.exampleCN: 他独自一人来参加晚宴。

items.meaning: a portion or role within a whole
items.meaningCN: 整体中的一份或一个角色
items.example: She played a part in the decision.
items.exampleCN: 她在这个决定中出了一份力。

items.structure: Latin portio, from the pars family
items.example: Each heir received an equal portion.
items.exampleCN: 每位继承人分得相等的一份。

items.meaning: a package; a portion of land
items.example: The land was sold in three parcels.
items.exampleCN: 这块地被分成三份出售。

latinEntries.meaning: a part, a share, a side
latinEntries.example: Pars is the root behind partner and portion.
latinEntries.exampleCN: pars 是 partner 与 portion 背后的词根。

latinEntries.example: Partire gave French partir and English partition.
latinEntries.exampleCN: partire 给出法语 partir 与英语 partition。

latinEntries.example: Partitionem is the source of Old French parçon.
latinEntries.exampleCN: partitionem 是古法语 parçon 的来源。

latinEntries.example: Particella became French parcelle and English parcel.
latinEntries.exampleCN: particella 演变为法语 parcelle 与英语 parcel。

intro.cn: silent 来自一个意为静止的拉丁语词。

items.en: Silentem meant being still or silent.

items.en: The word entered French as silent.
items.cn: 这个词以 silent 进入法语。

items.en: English borrowed it as silent.
items.cn: 英语借入时写作 silent。

items.en: It also described films without sound.
items.cn: 它也用来形容没有声音的电影。

note.en: Silent is compared with similar-looking words and with words for quiet.
note.cn: 把 silent 与形近词以及表示安静的词作比较。

definition_zh: 提醒；使想起；使联想到
definition_en: to make someone remember something they might forget, or to make them think of it
core_image: 有人轻轻碰一下你的胳膊，指着你差点忘掉的东西
scene: 出门前，母亲在门口叫住他，说下午还有一节牙医预约。 As he left, his mother reminded him of the dentist appointment that afternoon.
sceneCN: 这里 remind 是「提醒」（第 1 个义项：使某人记起可能会忘的事）；句意：他出门时，母亲提醒他下午还有牙医预约。

derivatives.zh: remind 加 -er 构成，义为「提醒；提示物」
remind 的第二成分，义为「心思；头脑」

senses.title: To make someone remember a duty
senses.definition: to tell someone about something they must do or must not forget
senses.definitionCN: 告诉某人必须做或不能忘记的事
senses.example: The nurse reminded him to take his pills after dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 护士提醒他晚饭后吃药。
senses.why: The word is a plain compound of re- and mind, so the picture is putting something back into someone's mind.
senses.whyCN: 这个词就是 re- 与 mind 的简单复合，画面是把某件事重新放进某人的心里。

senses.title: To make someone think of something
senses.definition: to cause someone to remember a person, place, or feeling through similarity
senses.definitionCN: 因相似而使人想起某个人、地方或感觉
senses.example: This song reminds me of my summer in the north.
senses.exampleCN: 这首歌让我想起在北方度过的那个夏天。
senses.why: A sight or sound can put a memory back into the mind without any duty involved, which is this sense.
senses.whyCN: 一个景象或声音可以不经任何职责，就把记忆重新放回心里，这就是第二义项。

intro.en: Remind is an English compound of the prefix re- and the native noun mind, first recorded in the seventeenth century.
intro.cn: remind 是英语本土复合词，由前缀 re- 与本土名词 mind 构成，最早见于十七世纪。

items.en: The noun gemynd means memory and mind, and becomes modern English mind.
items.cn: 古英语名词 gemynd 表示记忆与心智，后来演变为现代英语的 mind。

items.en: The prefix re- enters English through French and Latin and means again or back.
items.cn: 前缀 re- 经法语与拉丁语进入英语，表示「再次、回」。

items.en: Remind is formed to mean put a thing back into someone's mind.
items.cn: remind 被构造出来，表示「把某事重新放进某人心里」。

items.en: The pattern remind someone of something becomes established for similarity.
items.cn: 十八世纪，remind someone of something 这一句型固定下来，用于表示相似引起的联想。

items.en: The noun reminder turns the verb into a thing that prompts, such as an alarm or a note.
items.cn: 名词 reminder 把动词变成一个起提示作用的事物，例如闹钟或便条。

note.en: Remind is a native compound whose second half is mind, and it stands opposite remember in direction.
note.cn: remind 是第二个成分 mind 的本土复合词，与 remember 的方向相反。

entries.definition: something that makes you remember
entries.definitionCN: 提醒；提示物，由 remind 加 -er 构成

entries.definition: the part of a person that thinks and remembers
entries.definitionCN: 心智；头脑，是 remind 的第二成分

entries.definition: to keep or bring something into your own mind
entries.definitionCN: 记得；想起，与 remind 拼写相近但方向相反

entries.definition: to cause someone to do or say something
entries.definitionCN: 促使；提示，常用于舞台或软件

entries.definition: to warn someone about a danger or problem
entries.definitionCN: 向……报警；提醒注意，带有警告意味

entries.definition: to push someone gently, often to make them act
entries.definitionCN: 轻推；委婉提醒

normalIntro.en: Remind is simply re- plus mind, so the word means putting something back into a mind.
normalIntro.cn: remind 就是 re- 加 mind，意思是把某件事重新放回心里。

normal.en: Remember is what you do yourself; remind is what someone else does to you.
normal.cn: remember 是自己记得，remind 是别人来提醒你。

normal.en: Add -er for reminder, the thing that does the prompting.
normal.cn: 加 -er 得到 reminder，即起提示作用的事物。

normal.en: Remind someone of takes a noun, while remind someone to takes a verb.
normal.cn: remind sb of 后接名词，remind sb to 后接动词。

normal.en: A calendar alert is a digital reminder in everyday life.
normal.cn: 日历提醒就是日常生活中的数字 reminder。

normal.en: The second half is the native word mind, not the Latin root ment-.
normal.cn: 第二个成分是本土词 mind，而不是拉丁词根 ment-。

abstract.en: Picture a hand tapping your arm just as you reach for the wrong door.
abstract.cn: 想象你正要开错门时，一只手轻轻碰了碰你的胳膊。

abstract.en: See a yellow note stuck to a laptop screen.
abstract.cn: 想象笔记本电脑屏幕上贴着一张黄色便条。

abstract.en: Think of a smell that instantly brings back a kitchen from childhood.
abstract.cn: 想一种气味，瞬间把童年的厨房带回来。

examples.en: Please remind me to call the bank tomorrow.
examples.cn: 请提醒我明天给银行打电话。

examples.en: That photograph reminds her of her grandmother.
examples.cn: 那张照片让她想起她的祖母。

examples.en: The teacher reminded the class about the deadline.
examples.cn: 老师提醒全班注意截止日期。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞曼的」——想象瑞丽那位慢吞吞的人总被人轻轻提醒；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语本土复合词：前缀 re-（再次）加名词 mind（心智、记忆），字面即「重新放入心中」。

sensesIntro.en: Putting something back into a mind covers both a duty that must not be forgotten and a memory stirred by resemblance.
sensesIntro.cn: 把某事重新放进心里，既涵盖不能忘记的职责，也涵盖因相似而被唤起的回忆。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a light tap on the arm pointing at something nearly forgotten.
core.cn: 核心意象：有人轻碰你的胳膊，指向你差点忘掉的东西。

branches.en: A duty put back into the mind is the practical everyday sense.
branches.cn: 把职责重新放回心里，是最实际的日常义项。

branches.en: A sight that stirs a memory does the same work without any duty.
branches.cn: 触动记忆的景象做着同样的事，却与职责无关。

branches.en: Both are cases of something returning to mind from outside.
branches.cn: 两者都是某事物从外部回到心里的情形。

branches.en: Repeated reminders turn a prompt into a small warning.
branches.cn: 反复提醒会把提示变成小小的警告。

branches.en: Resemblance is the most common trigger of spontaneous recall.
branches.cn: 相似是最常见的自发回忆触发器。

intro.en: Remind is a rare case of a Latin prefix joined to a native English noun.
intro.cn: remind 是拉丁前缀与英语本土名词结合的少见例子。

latinIntro.en: The prefix re- means again, and mind is the native word for the thinking and remembering part of a person.
latinIntro.cn: 前缀 re- 表示「再次」，mind 是英语本族词，指人思考与记忆的部分。

items.example: Re- puts the thing back where it belongs.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 表示把它放回原处。

items.example: Mind is a native word of Germanic origin.
items.exampleCN: mind 是源自日耳曼语的本土词。

items.example: Reminder is the thing that prompts.
items.exampleCN: reminder 是起提示作用的事物。

items.example: Gemynd is the Old English ancestor of mind.
items.exampleCN: gemynd 是 mind 的古英语祖先。

items.meaning: a prompt or a note that reminds
items.example: A reminder can be a sound, a message, or a note.
items.exampleCN: reminder 可以是声音、消息或便条。

items.example: Mindful shows the noun mind with the ending -ful.
items.exampleCN: mindful 展示了名词 mind 加 -ful 的形式。

items.example: Memory is the Latin partner of the native mind.
items.exampleCN: memory 是本土词 mind 的拉丁对应词。

items.meaning: to keep or bring into your own mind
items.example: Remember reverses the direction of remind.
items.exampleCN: remember 与 remind 的方向相反。

definition_zh: 错误；过失；弄错；误认；误解
definition_en: a wrong act, decision or opinion, or the verb meaning to identify someone wrongly or to take words in the wrong sense
core_image: 手里拿着一把不属于自己的钥匙，插进锁孔却怎么也转不动
scene: 雨夜回家，楼道灯光昏暗，他把邻居的伞当成自己的拎了起来。 In the dim hallway he mistook his neighbour's umbrella for his own and carried it home.
sceneCN: 这里是「把…误认成」（第 3 个义项：认错了对象）；句意为昏暗楼道里，他把邻居的伞当成了自己的，一路拎回家。图中可辨识物件：湿淋淋的伞、昏黄的楼道灯、住户门牌。

derivatives.zh: 由 mistake 的过去分词转作形容词，义为「弄错的；错误的」
由 mistaken 加 -ly 构成，义为「错误地」
由 un- 加 mistake 加 -able 构成，义为「不会认错的；明显的」

senses.title: A wrong judgement or act
senses.definition: an act or decision that is wrong, or an opinion that does not match the facts
senses.definitionCN: 做错的事、错误的决定，或与事实不符的看法
senses.example: Leaving the gas on all night was a dangerous mistake.
senses.exampleCN: 让煤气整夜开着，是个危险的错误。
senses.why: Old Norse mistaka joined mis-, wrongly, to taka, to take, so a mistake is literally a wrong taking; the noun keeps that picture of a hand closing on the wrong thing.
senses.whyCN: 古诺斯语 mistaka 由 mis-（错）加 taka（拿、取）构成，字面就是「拿错」；名词把这幅画面留着——手合拢时抓住的不是想要的那件东西，于是留下一个做错的结果。

senses.title: A small error in written or spoken form
senses.definition: a slip in spelling, punctuation, calculation or pronunciation rather than a fault of judgement
senses.definitionCN: 拼写、标点、计算或发音上的小失误，而不是判断上的过错
senses.example: The essay was good except for two spelling mistakes.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章写得不错，只是有两处拼写错误。
senses.why: A wrong grasp can be small as well as large: a hand that writes the wrong letter has still taken the wrong shape, so the same noun covers slips on paper and failures in life.
senses.whyCN: 「拿错」既可以很大，也可以很小：写字的手取了错误的字形，仍是拿错了东西；于是同一个名词既管纸上的笔误，也管生活里的过失。

senses.title: To take one person or thing for another
senses.definition: to believe that a person or thing is someone or something else, especially because they look similar
senses.definitionCN: 以为某人或某物是另一个人或另一件东西，尤因两者相像
senses.example: From the back of the hall she mistook me for my cousin.
senses.exampleCN: 在礼堂后排，她把我误认成了我表弟。
senses.why: Here the old compound is still visible: mis- says the taking is wrong, and the verb names the moment the eyes take one face and file it under another name.
senses.whyCN: 这里古诺斯语的构词还看得见：mis- 说明这一「取」取错了，动词命名的正是眼睛把一张脸拿了去、却归到另一个名字下的那一刻。

senses.title: To give someone's words the wrong meaning
senses.definition: to understand a remark or an intention in a way the speaker did not mean
senses.definitionCN: 把某句话或某种用意理解成说话人并未表达的意思
senses.example: Do not mistake my quietness for indifference.
senses.exampleCN: 别把我的沉默当成冷漠。
senses.why: The mind also takes: it receives words and stores a sense, and when the stored sense is not the one offered, English reuses the mis- plus take pattern and calls it a mistake of meaning.
senses.whyCN: 心智也在「取」：它接住话语、存下一个意思；存下的不是对方给出的那一个，英语便再次动用 mis- 加「取」的旧模式，把这叫意思上的拿错。

intro.en: Mistake came from a Norse compound of a prefix meaning wrongly and a verb meaning to take, and English first used it as a verb before it named the error itself.
intro.cn: mistake 来自古诺斯语中「表示错误的前缀＋表示拿取的动词」的复合体；英语先把它当动词用，后来才用它指错误本身。

items.en: The verb mistaka joined mis-, wrongly, to taka, to take, and meant to seize the wrong thing or to misjudge a matter.
items.cn: 动词 mistaka 把表示「错」的 mis- 与表示「拿」的 taka 合在一起，意为拿错了东西或把事情判断错了。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the fourteenth century as mistaken, first in the sense of understanding a matter wrongly.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语借入这个动词，写作 mistaken，最早指把一件事理解错了。

items.en: A noun grew beside the verb, at first naming a wrong deed and later any small slip of hand or pen.
items.cn: 动词旁边长出一个名词，最初指做错的事，后来也指手上或笔下的任何小失误。

items.en: The phrase by mistake fixed the noun as the ordinary way of saying that something was done without intention.
items.cn: by mistake 这个说法把名词固定下来，成为表示「并非有意」的常用说法。

items.en: Modern English keeps the count noun and the verb alive and adds fixed patterns such as mistake A for B and a spelling mistake.
items.cn: 现代英语同时保留可数名词与动词，并发展出 mistake A for B、a spelling mistake 这类固定说法。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the same Norse stem through derived forms and the shared prefix; the near-meaning group gathers other words for going wrong.
note.cn: 形近组沿着同一个古诺斯语词干，收它的派生形式与共用的前缀；近义组收其他表示出错、走偏的词。

entries.definition: The past participle of mistake used as an adjective, meaning wrong in judgement or wrongly identified.
entries.definitionCN: mistake 的过去分词转作形容词，指判断有误或被误认的。

entries.definition: Built with un- and -able on mistake: too clear to be taken for anything else.
entries.definitionCN: 在 mistake 上加 un- 与 -able 构成，指清楚得不可能认错。

entries.definition: A prefix meaning wrongly, the element that turns a taking into a mistake.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「错误地」的前缀，正是它把一次「拿取」变成了拿错。

entries.definition: A wrong result or a departure from what is correct, often in calculation or judgement.
entries.definitionCN: 错误的结果或偏离正确之处，常用于计算或判断。

entries.definition: A careless and serious mistake, usually one that is embarrassing.
entries.definitionCN: 粗心而严重的错误，往往令人难堪。

entries.definition: A small mistake made by not paying attention.
entries.definitionCN: 因没留神而造成的小错。

normalIntro.en: The word began as a Norse verb of taking, and the whole family keeps the picture of a hand reaching for the wrong object.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从古诺斯语中一个「拿取」的动词开始，整个词族都留着伸手抓错东西的画面。

normal.en: The Norse verb was mis- plus taka, to take, so a mistake is first of all something taken wrongly.
normal.cn: 古诺斯语动词是 mis- 加 taka（拿），所以 mistake 首先是拿错了的东西。

normal.en: The same stem explains mistook and mistaken: one is the wrong take in the past, the other the state of having taken wrongly.
normal.cn: 同一词干也解释 mistook 与 mistaken：前者是过去的拿错，后者是已经拿错的状态。

normal.en: A spelling mistake is the smallest version of the picture: the hand takes the wrong letter.
normal.cn: spelling mistake 是这幅画最小的版本：手取错了字母。

normal.en: Mistake A for B puts two nouns on either side because the verb needs both the person seen and the name given.
normal.cn: mistake A for B 两边各放一个名词，因为动词既需要被看见的人，也需要被安上的名字。

normal.en: Mistakenly adds -ly, turning the error into the manner of an action.
normal.cn: mistakenly 加 -ly，把错误变成动作的方式。

abstract.en: A word built out of taking reminds us that most errors begin as a confident grab, not as doubt.
abstract.cn: 一个由「拿」造出的词提醒人：多数错误起于自信的一抓，而不是怀疑。

abstract.en: The distance between mistook and mistaken is the distance between doing and being: first the wrong grab, then the wrong state.
abstract.cn: mistook 与 mistaken 之间的距离，就是做与是的距离：先有错抓，再有错的状态。

abstract.en: In every mistake there is an intention that ran ahead of the facts.
abstract.cn: 每个 mistake 里都有一个跑在事实前面的意图。

examples.en: Everyone makes a mistake now and then.
examples.cn: 人偶尔都会犯错。

examples.en: He mistook the quiet street for a dead end.
examples.cn: 他把那条安静的街道误当成死胡同。

examples.en: A single spelling mistake can change the whole sentence.
examples.cn: 一个拼写错误就能改变整句话的意思。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「迷死忒克」——迷糊到极点就伸手拿错；记住 mistake 是弄错。

root: 古诺斯语 mistaka ＝ mis-（错）＋ taka（拿、取），本义「拿错、误取」，十四世纪进入英语。属北日耳曼语来源，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a wrong taking; from it grow the wrong act, the slip on paper, the misidentified person and the misread sentence.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「拿错」；由此长出做错的事、纸上的小失误、认错的人以及听错的话。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand closing on the wrong object while the wanted one stays on the shelf.
core.cn: 核心意象：手合拢时抓住的是一件错的东西，想要的那件还留在架上。

branches.en: a hand grabbing the wrong tool in a hurry
branches.cn: 匆忙中抓住了一件不顺手的工具

branches.en: a red circle around one letter on a page
branches.cn: 纸上一个字母被红笔圈住

branches.en: a stranger's umbrella taken in a dim hallway
branches.cn: 昏暗楼道里被拿走的陌生人的伞

branches.en: a kind remark heard as a cold one
branches.cn: 一句好意被听成了冷话

branches.en: a teacher counting errors before writing a comment
branches.cn: 老师先数错处再写评语

intro.en: The word is a Norse compound of a prefix and a verb of taking, carried into English noun and adjective forms by English endings.
intro.cn: 这个词是古诺斯语中「前缀＋拿取动词」的复合体，再靠英语词尾变成名词与形容词形式。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for mistake; the word belongs to the Norse side of Germanic, and the similar Latin capere is not its source.
latinIntro.cn: mistake 没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；它属于日耳曼语中的北支，形似的拉丁语 capere 并不是它的来源。

definition_zh: 交换；兑换；（证券交易所等）交易场所；短暂交谈；交换所
definition_en: the act of giving one thing and receiving another in its place
core_image: 两手同时伸出，各自把东西递到对方掌心，收回时已换了一样
scene: 车站门口，两个旅客把各自的车票递过去，看对方的座位是否更靠窗。 They agreed to an exchange of seats so the child could sit by the window.
sceneCN: 这里 exchange 指「两方互给互取的交换」（第 1 个义项：作为一次对等交换）；句意为他们同意换座位，好让孩子靠窗坐。

pos.zh: 交换；兑换；交易场所；短暂交谈

derivatives.zh: exchange + -able（可…的）→ 可交换的；可兑换的
inter-（相互）+ change → 互换；换乘站
interchange + -able → 可互换的
拉丁 cambiare（交换）经古法语 → 改变；零钱（同根，语义分叉为「变」）
bureau + de + change → 外币兑换处（法语借入）
exchange + -er → 交换器（如热交换器）

senses.title: Giving one thing for another
senses.definition: the act of giving something and receiving something else in return
senses.definitionCN: 给出某物并换回另一物的行为
senses.example: They agreed to an exchange of seats so the child could sit by the window.
senses.exampleCN: 他们同意换座位，好让孩子靠窗坐。
senses.why: Latin ex- 'out' plus cambiare 'to barter' gives a giving out that is answered by a taking in.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 ex-「出」加 cambiare「以物易物」，给出一个「给出」并由「取回」回应的动作。

senses.title: A venue for trading securities or currencies
senses.titleCN: 证券或货币的交易场所
senses.definition: an organized market where financial instruments or currencies are bought and sold
senses.definitionCN: 买卖金融工具或货币的有组织市场
senses.example: The exchange closed early when the storm cut the power.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨切断电力，交易所提前收盘。
senses.why: A place where values are exchanged takes the name of the act, and the act becomes a building.
senses.whyCN: 交换价值的地方取了动作之名，动作也就成了一座建筑。

senses.title: An exchange of letters or remarks
senses.definition: a series of communications between two parties, as an exchange of letters or views
senses.definitionCN: 两方之间一系列的书信或意见往来
senses.example: The exchange of letters lasted three years and settled nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 书信往来进行三年，什么也没解决。
senses.why: Words are given and words are returned, so correspondence is the same shape as trade.
senses.whyCN: 话被给出，话又被送回，因此通信与交易是同一个形状。

senses.title: A short argument or conversation
senses.definition: a brief, often heated, passage of talk between two people
senses.definitionCN: 两人之间一段简短、常带火气的对话
senses.example: A sharp exchange at the door ended the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 门口一场尖锐的交锋结束了这次会面。
senses.why: The countable sense shrinks a whole correspondence into one round of give and take.
senses.whyCN: 可数义把整段往来缩小为一个给出与回敬的回合。

senses.title: A telephone switchboard
senses.definition: dated technical: a building or apparatus where lines are connected by an operator
senses.definitionCN: 旧技术用语：由话务员接通线路的机房或设备
senses.example: The old exchange on the corner still has a manual board.
senses.exampleCN: 街角那间旧交换机房仍有一台人工交换台。
senses.why: Lines are exchanged between callers, and the machinery that performs the exchange takes the name.
senses.whyCN: 线路在通话者之间被交换，执行交换的机器便取了这个名字。

senses.title: A swap of captives or personnel
senses.definition: an agreed handing over of prisoners, spies or personnel by two sides
senses.definitionCN: 两方商定的战俘、间谍或人员交还
senses.example: The prisoner exchange took place at a border bridge at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 战俘交换在黎明时分的一座边境桥上进行。
senses.why: People are treated as the things given and received, which is why the plain word is used without euphemism.
senses.whyCN: 人被当作被给出与接收的对象，因此这里直用这个普通的词，不加委婉语。

senses.title: To swap (verb)
senses.definition: to give something and receive something else in return, or to give each other
senses.definitionCN: 给出某物并换回另一物，或互相给予
senses.example: The two schools exchange students every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这两所学校每年春天交换学生。
senses.why: The verb makes the noun into a repeated or mutual act.
senses.whyCN: 动词把这个名词变成反复或相互的动作。

senses.title: Conversion of one currency for another
senses.definition: the changing of money of one country into that of another at a stated rate
senses.definitionCN: 按既定比价把一国货币换为另一国货币
senses.example: The exchange cost him nine percent before he left the airport.
senses.exampleCN: 他还没出机场，兑换就花掉了他百分之九。
senses.why: A money counter is the same gesture with one currency on each side, so no separate word is needed.
senses.whyCN: 换钱的柜台是同一个动作，只是两侧各放一种货币，因此无需另造新词。

senses.title: An organized programme of visits
senses.definition: a scheme in which people from two places visit each other, as a student or cultural exchange
senses.definitionCN: 两地人员互访的安排，如学生交流或文化交流
senses.example: The cultural exchange brought twelve potters to the city for a month.
senses.exampleCN: 这项文化交流把十二位陶工请到城里住了一个月。
senses.why: An institution borrows the word for reciprocal visits, since each side hosts and is hosted.
senses.whyCN: 一种制度借用了这个词来指互访，因为每一方既接待也被接待。

intro.en: Exchange is a French-shaped verb from spoken Latin, and its key root is one of the least certain in this batch.
intro.cn: exchange 是一个由口语拉丁而来、带法语形态的动词，其核心词根是本批中最不确定的几个之一。

items.en: Cambiare meant 'to exchange, to barter'. Its own origin is uncertain: a link to a Celtic verb for 'change' is often suggested, but no derivation has been demonstrated.
items.cn: cambiare 意为「交换、以物易物」。它自身的来源不确定：常有人提出它与某个凯尔特语表「改变」的动词有关，但没有任何派生得到证实。

items.en: Spoken Latin added ex- 'out' to cambiare, producing *excambiare 'to exchange out, to swap'.
items.cn: 口语拉丁给 cambiare 加上 ex-「出」，构成 *excambiare「换出、交换」。

items.en: Old French eschangier continues the spoken form and supplies the -ch- that English preserves in the noun.
items.cn: 古法语 eschangier 承接口语形式，并提供英语名词中保留的那个 -ch-。

items.en: English borrows the word in the fourteenth century as both noun and verb, first for swapping goods and then for money changing.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪把这个词作为名词与动词一并借入，先指换货，后指换钱。

items.en: The financial sense develops with the rise of the bourse: a place where bills and currencies are exchanged becomes simply the exchange.
items.cn: 金融义随交易所的兴起而发展：买卖票据与货币的场所干脆就被称作 the exchange。

items.en: The telephone exchange extends the word to a room where lines are connected, a sense now largely historical.
items.cn: 电话交换机把这个词扩展到接通线路的机房，这一义项如今大体已成历史。

note.en: The first group shares the root or the shape and is easily confused; the second holds words for swaps and for trading venues.
note.cn: 第一组共享词根或外形，容易混淆；第二组是交换行为与交易场所的其他说法。

entries.definition: The short form of the same Latin root, but it means to become different as well as to swap; exchange keeps only the two-way giving.
entries.definitionCN: 同一拉丁词根的短形式，但除交换外还指「变得不同」；exchange 只保留双向给予之义。

entries.definition: Inter- 'between' plus change marks a two-way swap, and in transport it names a junction where routes swap passengers.
entries.definitionCN: inter-「之间」加 change 标出双向互换，在交通中指路线互换乘客的枢纽。

entries.definition: The adjective means able to be swapped or converted, often in economics or law rather than in daily speech.
entries.definitionCN: 这个形容词指可交换或可兑换，多见于经济或法律语境而非日常口语。

entries.definition: A tax on goods, from a different Latin source (ex- plus caedere 'to cut'); it has nothing to do with swapping.
entries.definitionCN: 指货物税，来自另一个拉丁来源（ex- 加 caedere「切」），与交换无关。

entries.definition: The everyday word for a mutual exchange, usually of similar things and often without paperwork.
entries.definitionCN: 互相交换的日常用词，通常换同类之物，且常无手续。

entries.definition: An exchange carried on as business, especially of goods; exchange is neutral about whether money is involved.
entries.definitionCN: 作为生意的交换，尤指货物；exchange 不限定是否涉及钱。

entries.definition: Exchange with no money at all; it is one strict kind of exchange.
entries.definitionCN: 完全不用钱的交换，是 exchange 的一个严格子类。

entries.definition: Changing one thing into another form, often without a second party; exchange requires someone on the other side.
entries.definitionCN: 把一物变为另一形式，常无第二方；exchange 则要求对面有人。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ex- 'out' + cambiare 'barter': hand something out and take something in.
normal.cn: ex-「出」+ cambiare「以物易物」：把东西递出去，再收一件回来。

normal.en: The family runs exchange, exchangeable, interchange, interchangeable, changer, change.
normal.cn: 同族词有 exchange、exchangeable、interchange、interchangeable、changer、change。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the venues: stock exchange, exchange rate, labour exchange, telephone exchange.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出场所：证券交易所、汇率、职业介绍所、电话交换机。

normal.en: The verb is mutual: two schools exchange students, and each is host and guest.
normal.cn: 动词是相互的：两校交换学生，各自既是主人也是客人。

normal.en: Words exchange too: an exchange of views is correspondence with the same shape.
normal.cn: 话也能交换：交换意见就是同形状的往来。

abstract.en: Picture two palms opening at the same moment, each now holding what the other had.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手掌同时张开，各自握着对方原来拿的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a building with no goods in it, only numbers being swapped all day.
abstract.cn: 想象一座里面没有货物、整天只在交换数字的建筑。

abstract.en: Picture an operator plugging a line into a socket so two strangers can talk.
abstract.cn: 想象话务员把一根线插进插孔，好让两个陌生人通话。

examples.en: The two museums arranged an exchange of paintings for a season.
examples.cn: 两家博物馆安排了一季的绘画互换。

examples.en: He exchanged his seat for a place by the aisle and slept the whole way.
examples.cn: 他换到靠过道的座位，一路睡了过去。

examples.en: The exchange rate moved two percent before the markets opened.
examples.cn: 开市之前，汇率已经动了两成中的两个百分点。

dict_mnemonic.text: ex（出）+ change（换）＝ 把东西换出去，换回一样；先记「两只手同时递」，再记「一所房子专门换数字」。

root: 拉丁 cambiare「交换、以物易物」+ ex-「出」→ 口语拉丁 *excambiare → 古法语 eschangier → 英语 exchange；cambiare 来源不确定，与凯尔特语的联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one gesture of give and take: a swap, a hall of swaps, words swapped, one sharp round of words, a switchboard, captives handed over, the verb, currency conversion, and a programme of mutual visits.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿一个「递出与接回」的动作展开：一次交换、专门交换的场所、交换话语、一个尖锐的话语回合、交换机、交出俘虏、动词、货币兑换，以及互访项目。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands opening at once, each receiving exactly what the other releases.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手同时张开，各自接到的正是对方松开的。

branches.en: THE GESTURE AND THE VERB: one completed swap, then the same act performed habitually or mutually.
branches.cn: 动作与动词：一次完成的交换，再是同一动作被反复或相互地做。

branches.en: PLACES AND MACHINES OF SWAPPING: a hall for securities, a room for telephone lines, a counter for currencies.
branches.cn: 交换的场所与机器：换证券的大厅、接线路的机房、换货币的柜台。

branches.en: WORDS IN PLACE OF GOODS: correspondence over years, or one sharp round at a door.
branches.cn: 以话代货：经年的通信，或门口一个尖锐的回合。

branches.en: PEOPLE HANDED OVER: the plain word is used without euphemism for prisoners.
branches.cn: 被交出的人：对俘虏直接用这个普通的词，不加委婉。

branches.en: AN INSTITUTION OF HOSTING: each side gives a visit and receives one, so a programme becomes an exchange.
branches.cn: 接待的制度：每一方给出一次访问也收到一次，于是项目本身成了 exchange。

intro.en: Exchange is one Latin prefix plus one uncertain Latin verb, and both parts recur in English words about movement and substitution.
intro.cn: exchange 是一个拉丁前缀加一个来源不确定的拉丁动词，两部分在英语中反复出现于表移动与替代的词里。

latinIntro.en: Latin cambiare 'to barter' gives change, exchange, interchange and the money-changing phrases; ex- 'out' recurs in exit, export and extract. The root behind cambiare is not established.

definition_zh: 方式；方法；举止；态度；礼貌；礼节；风格；手法
definition_en: the way in which something is done, a person's bearing towards others, polite social behaviour in the plural, or a recognizable style in art
core_image: 同一只手，握杯子时轻，握锤子时重，落下的力道各不相同
scene: 画室的长桌上摆着同一只杯子的三幅画稿，每一幅落笔的轻重都不一样。 He stirred the paint in a slow, deliberate manner before the first stroke.
sceneCN: 这里 manner 是「方式、方法」（第 1 个义项：做某件事时所采取的样子）；句意为他在落第一笔之前，以缓慢而有意的方式搅动颜料。图中可辨识物件：三幅杯子画稿、颜料碟、长桌。

pos.zh: 方式；方法；举止；态度；礼貌；风格

derivatives.zh: 由 manner 加表示「做法、主义」的后缀 -ism 构成，义为「习惯性的小动作；（艺术上的）风格主义」
由 manner 加 -ly 构成，义为「有礼貌的；举止得体的」
由 manner 加 -ed 构成，义为「举止不自然的；做作的」

senses.title: The way something is done
senses.definition: the way in which something is done, happens or is arranged
senses.definitionCN: 某事被做、发生或安排时所呈现的样子
senses.example: She answered every question in a calm, even manner that quieted the room.
senses.exampleCN: 她以平静而匀称的方式回答每一个问题，让整个房间安静下来。
senses.why: The word descends from Latin manus, hand; manner is literally the way a thing is handled, so the shape of the doing is what it names first.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自拉丁语 manus（手）；manner 字面上就是「一样东西被手握持的样子」，所以它最先命名的就是做事的形状。

senses.title: A person's bearing towards others
senses.definition: the way a person behaves, speaks or carries themselves in front of other people
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在他人面前表现、说话、举手投足的样子
senses.example: His easy manner made strangers feel they had known him for years.
senses.exampleCN: 他随和的举止让陌生人觉得已经认识他多年。
senses.why: Handling a person is as physical as handling an object, so the way you hold yourself in company also became a manner.
senses.whyCN: 待人接物和处理物件一样带着身体感，于是你在人前拿住自己的那种姿态，也成了一种 manner。

senses.title: Polite social behaviour, chiefly in the plural
senses.definition: the polite habits and rules of behaviour that a society expects, usually used in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 一个社会所期待的那套礼貌习惯与行为规矩，通常以复数出现
senses.example: The children were taught to mind their manners at the table.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们被教导在餐桌旁要讲究礼貌。
senses.why: One manner is a single way of acting; once a society agrees on the approved ways, they are counted up as manners, and the plural marks a set of rules.
senses.whyCN: 单个 manner 是一种做法；一旦社会就「哪些做法被认可」达成一致，它们就被一条条数出来成了 manners，复数标出的是一整套规矩。

senses.title: A recognizable style in art or writing
senses.definition: the personal or period style that marks a work of art, writing or music
senses.definitionCN: 标在一件艺术品、文字或音乐上的个人风格或时代风格
senses.example: The late portraits were painted in the manner of his old teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 那些晚期肖像是以他旧日老师的手法画成的。
senses.why: If manner is the way a hand moves, a painter's repeated handling of paint is recognized as that painter's manner, and style follows from the same observation.
senses.whyCN: 如果 manner 是一只手动作的样子，那么一位画家反复处理颜料的方式就会被人认作他的 manner，「风格」的意思便从同一种观察里长出来。

intro.en: Manner comes from a Latin adjective built on the word for hand, and it passed through French before English used it for ways, bearing, politeness and style.
intro.cn: manner 出自一个建立在「手」这个词上的拉丁形容词，经法语中转之后，才在英语里用来指方式、举止、礼貌与风格。

items.en: Manus, the Latin noun for hand, supplied the base for a whole family of words about handling and the way things are held.
items.cn: 拉丁语名词 manus 意为手，为了一整族关于摆弄以及握持方式的词提供了词基。

items.en: A Vulgar Latin adjective manuarius, of the hand, is generally taken as the link; it described what belongs to the hand or the way it holds something.
items.cn: 一般认为俗拉丁语形容词 manuarius（手的）是中间环节；它描述属于手的，或手握持某物的方式。

items.en: Old French maniere meant way, sort or kind, and it carried the word into English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语 maniere 意为方式、种类，在诺曼时期之后把这个词带进英语。

items.en: Middle English maner covered way, custom and behaviour, and the modern spelling manner settled later under French influence.
items.cn: 中古英语 maner 兼指方式、习俗与行为，现代拼写 manner 后来在法语影响下固定下来。

items.en: Modern English keeps manner for ways and bearing, counts the plural manners as polite behaviour, and lets art criticism use it for a personal stroke.
items.cn: 现代英语保留 manner 指方式与举止，把复数 manners 用作礼貌行为，也让艺术评论用它指个人的笔法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers derivatives and words built on the Latin noun for hand; the near group gathers nouns for ways of doing and ways of carrying oneself.
note.cn: 形近组收派生词以及建立在拉丁语「手」这个名词上的词；近义组收表示做事方式与自我呈现方式的名称。

entries.definition: A habitual gesture or way of speaking, or an exaggerated style in art.
entries.definitionCN: 习惯性的动作或说话方式；也指艺术上夸张做作的风格；由 manner 加 -ism 构成。

entries.definition: Showing good manners; polite.
entries.definitionCN: 有礼貌的；举止得体的；由 manner 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: Behaving in an artificial or exaggerated way.
entries.definitionCN: 举止做作、不自然的；由 manner 加 -ed 构成。

entries.definition: Done with the hands, or a handbook; from Latin manus, hand.
entries.definitionCN: 用手做的；也指手册；出自拉丁语 manus（手），与 manner 同源。

entries.definition: The method or style in which something is done.
entries.definitionCN: 做某事所采用的方法或样式。

entries.definition: A planned and regular way of doing something.
entries.definitionCN: 有计划、有步骤的做事方式。

entries.definition: A distinctive way of doing, writing or designing.
entries.definitionCN: 独特的做事、写作或设计方式。

entries.definition: The way a person stands, moves or carries themselves.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人站立、走动或自我呈现的姿态。

entries.definition: The outward behaviour and appearance a person shows to others.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人在他人面前表现出的外在举止与神情。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on the Latin noun for hand, and its family keeps returning to handling, bearing, social rules and the personal stroke of an artist.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语表示「手」的名词上，它的同族词反复回到握持、姿态、社交规矩，以及艺术家的个人笔法。

normal.en: Latin manus means hand, and the Vulgar Latin manuarius, of the hand, is the usual link to French maniere, a way or kind.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 manus 意为手，俗拉丁语 manuarius（手的）通常是通向法语 maniere（方式、种类）的中间环节。

normal.en: Manner is therefore the look of a thing being handled, which explains why it can name a method and a bearing at once.
normal.cn: 所以 manner 就是「一样东西被握持时的样子」，这解释了它为何既能指方法，又能指姿态。

normal.en: Manners became a separate plural word because polite behaviour is learned as a set of approved ways.
normal.cn: manners 成为独立的复数词，是因为礼貌行为是作为一整套被认可的做法学来的。

normal.en: Mannerism and mannerly both grow straight out of manner, one naming a habit, the other naming good behaviour.
normal.cn: mannerism 与 mannerly 都直接从 manner 长出来，一个指习惯动作，一个指得体的举止。

normal.en: The phrase in a manner of speaking marks the method sense, softened into a polite hedge.
normal.cn: 短语 in a manner of speaking 标出了「方式」这层意思，又被磨成一句客气的退让。

abstract.en: A hand's pressure is never twice the same, and that difference is what the word first names.
abstract.cn: 一只手落下的力道从不完全相同，而这点差别正是这个词最先命名的东西。

abstract.en: Method, bearing and politeness are one idea at three distances: how a thing is held, how a body is held, how a self is held.
abstract.cn: 方法、姿态与礼貌是同一个念头在三个距离上：东西怎么被握，身体怎么被摆，自己怎么被端住。

abstract.en: Style is only manner that has become recognizable enough to carry a name.
abstract.cn: 风格不过是已经明显到足以拥有名字的那种 manner。

examples.en: She answered every question in a calm, even manner that quieted the room.
examples.cn: 她以平静而匀称的方式回答每一个问题，让整个房间安静下来。

examples.en: The children were taught to mind their manners at the table.
examples.cn: 孩子们被教导在餐桌旁要讲究礼貌。

examples.en: The late portraits were painted in the manner of his old teacher.
examples.cn: 那些晚期肖像是以他旧日老师的手法画成的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「曼纳」——曼纳端水时手势很讲究，一举一动都合礼数；记住 manner 是方式、举止，复数 manners 是礼貌。

root: 拉丁语 manus（手）→ 俗拉丁语 manuarius（手的）→ 古法语 maniere（方式、种类）→ 中古英语 maner → 英语 manner。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the shape of a hand's handling; the senses then divide into the way a thing is done, a person's bearing, agreed social politeness and an artist's stroke.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一只手握持动作的形状；义项由此分成做事的方式、个人的姿态、社会约定的礼节，以及艺术家的笔法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand holding a cup lightly and a hammer heavily, the pressure never the same.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一只手，握杯轻、握锤重，落下的力道各不相同。

branches.en: a hand stirring paint before the first stroke
branches.cn: 落笔前搅动颜料的一只手

branches.en: three sketches of one cup on a long table
branches.cn: 长桌上同一只杯子的三幅画稿

branches.en: a stranger greeted with an easy smile
branches.cn: 用随和笑容迎接陌生人

branches.en: children seated and waiting for the meal
branches.cn: 孩子们坐好等着开饭

branches.en: a painter's repeated stroke on late portraits
branches.cn: 画家在晚期肖像上重复的笔法

intro.en: A Latin noun for hand, a Vulgar Latin adjective of the hand, one French borrowing and three English suffixes carry manner from grip to bearing, politeness and style.
intro.cn: 一个表示「手」的拉丁名词、一个意为「手的」俗拉丁形容词、一次法语借入，再加三个英语词尾，把 manner 从握持带到姿态、礼貌与风格。

latinIntro.en: Latin manus is recorded and reliable, and the Vulgar Latin adjective manuarius is generally accepted as the bridge to Old French maniere.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 manus 有记录且可靠，俗拉丁语形容词 manuarius 一般被认为是通向古法语 maniere 的桥。
